title: From making friends to managing money: Students' advice for this year's freshers
description: BC News asked current students about the worries they had before arriving at university how they overcame them.
author: Grace Dean
content:
While they were excited to start university, students say they worried about budgeting, making friends and being homesick
You've got your A-level results and your university place has been confirmed.
But while you may be excited about exploring a new city, meeting new friends and studying a subject you love - you might also be a bit anxious about what comes next.
With a record number of 18-year-olds expected to start university this year, BBC News asked current students what advice they'd give to freshers feeling uncertain about the big changes ahead.
For Isaak Hewitt, moving to Cardiff for university - where he knew no-one - was a "completely blank slate".
The idea of meeting lots of new people for the first time since starting secondary school was nerve-racking he says, but Isaak made friends by talking to people he met at lectures and seminars. Now aged 20, Isaak says he was sometimes "terrified" trying to strike up conversations, but the fact everyone was studying English together gave them common ground.
He advises freshers to act confident - even if you're scared inside - and to put yourself out there.
Many people say making friends is one of their biggest worries about starting uni
As a commuter student in Nottingham, Grace Morrell was also worried about how she'd meet people, when others were making friends through their halls and student flats. Instead, Grace says she met new people by joining her student magazine, and the radio and theatre societies.
"A lot of my friendships come from putting myself out there and just doing what I love, which I found was a bit hard at times, especially when you don't know anyone," says Grace, 19.
'I worked really hard and it paid off': Elation, nerves and proud parents as students get results
Are the UK's top universities really 'hoovering up' students?
Lots of students try to connect with future coursemates and flatmates on social media before they start university, like Mustafa Dassu, 19, who says freshers' WhatsApp chats helped him make friends before he started at King's College London.
"Everyone was typing on them all the time between that period of results day and freshers' itself," Mustafa says, "and I met friends that I'm still in touch with a lot today."
"I really worried about having to be on my own," says Izzy Garcez, 20, who thought she would miss spending evenings with her family and having people to eat and watch TV with.
But in the end she wasn't as homesick as she'd anticipated.
"Realistically, you'll make friends so quickly at uni," Izzy says, "and you're going to get to a point where you realise 'I've not called my parents in a week', and you'll realise that suddenly you're not actually missing them anymore - or not missing them nearly as much."
Kieran says it's important to remember your maintenance loan has to last until the next instalment
Journalism student Kieran Miller was worried about money, but he compared student bank accounts and chose one that gave him a free 16-25 Railcard, and signed up for student discount schemes.
Everything you need to know about university costs
Though it might be exciting to see your first maintenance loan payment hit your bank account in one big lump sum, Kieran, 19, says you need to remember it has to last until the next instalment.
With the help of his mum, Kieran, from Swansea, made a provisional budget before moving away, but warns that it's easy to get caught up in the student experience and spend more than you planned to.
"When you start uni and you're living away from your family and you've got this new sense of freedom it was also really difficult to stay strict financially because you want to make mates with people," he says. "Someone might invite you to go for food or to go for a drink - and you're like, 'I don't really want to say no because this is a chance to connect with someone.'"
As well as student loans, most universities offer a variety of scholarships and bursaries, and it's worth checking whether you're eligible.
Many students balance classes and studying alongside part-time work, volunteering, sports clubs and societies.
Before starting her English and drama degree, Avery Hewitt, 19, worried about juggling studying with working and playing in a university band. She says speaking online to a student ambassador about the workload helped her manage her expectations.
Avery also advises new students to be realistic about their timetable and how much they can take on.
"I threw myself into everything in the first semester, which I quickly figured out was too much to handle," Avery says, "so I had to make responsible choices about what societies or club nights I needed to cut back on."
Pia switched from biochemistry to film and English
Even though your place is now confirmed, it's still not too late to change your mind. You can contact your university before you start to ask about changing course, or you can apply for courses at other universities through clearing.
After she started at the University of East Anglia, Pia Subong, 21, says she realised that biochemistry wasn't the right course for her and so switched to film and English.
If you're having doubts about whether the course is right for you, "you're having these feelings for a reason," Pia says.
Fatima says taking a gap year was the right decision for her
You can also take a gap year, as Fatima Qureshi, 19, from London did - because she wasn't sure which course she wanted to do or which career path she'd enjoy.
Fatima eventually decided to study law, but if she had chosen a course the year previously she'd likely have opted for biochemistry or pharmacy.
"It was the best thing I could have done," she says.
It's natural to feel anxious, according to Mel Kennedy, student wellbeing adviser at Ulster University, who says change "can be scary" and lots of people experience "fear of the unknown".
"For many students, starting university is the first time that they're stepping into a genuinely unknown environment," agrees Lindsay While, assistant director for student wellbeing and welfare at Teesside University.
"Many students do experience anxiety and uncertainty because it is such a major transition, but everybody's experience is completely different."
Universities offer a range of practical and wellbeing services, including budgeting advice, financial support, counselling and study support sessions. You can also reach out to the university if you need support before you start.
Some people told BBC News university had felt like the expected next step after sixth form or college. But Aashi Soni, 20, from Leicester, knew it wasn't right for her.
"Your college and sixth form don't really push you down that path [of apprenticeships] like they do with university and I found it really difficult," Aashi says. She turned down her university offers and took a gap year to find a suitable apprenticeship.
In the end, Aashi started a Level 6 degree apprenticeship in sales at Coca-Cola Europacific Partners. She says it has helped her grow in confidence, gain real-life experience while studying, and get mentoring.
Aashi and Meenu say university is often presented as the default option - but it wasn't right for them
Meenu Hettigama, 21, from Walsall began a creative media course after leaving school, but soon dropped out and applied for apprenticeships instead. She is now two years into a management degree apprenticeship at Amazon.
"University is not the only pathway," Meenu says, "even if maybe you think it's the most conventional or it is what your family want you to do."
You can search for apprenticeships on the UK government, Welsh government, Northern Ireland government and apprenticeships.scot websites. You can also find apprenticeships on sites like LinkedIn and Indeed and at apprenticeship recruitment events.

title: Pakistan embassy unveils Qu­aid’s statue in Washington
description: The statue, donated by the Quaid-i-Azam Foundation of Houston, will remain permanently at the embassy.
author: Anwar Iqbal
content:
WASHINGTON: A statue of Qu­aid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah was unveiled at the Pakistan Embassy in Washington on Friday, giving the country’s Independence Day celebrations a distinctly historical dimension and placing the founder of Pakis­tan at the centre of a ceremony that also highlighted the evolving Pakistan-United States relationship.
Ambassador of Pakistan to the US Rizwan Saeed Sheikh unvei­led the statue during an Indepen­dence Day ceremony attended by members of the Pakistani-American community, diplomats and media representatives.
The statue, donated by the Quaid-i-Azam Foundation of Houston, will remain permanently at the embassy. Its unveiling comes as Pakistan prepares to mark Jinnah’s 150th birth anniversary later this year.
Paying tribute to the founder, Ambassador Sheikh said the nati­­on remained grateful to Mr Jin­nah for his constitutional struggle and tireless efforts that turned the idea of Pakistan into a reality.
“The inspiring leadership of Quaid-i-Azam united the Muslims of the subcontinent under one flag and blessed us with freedom,” he said, urging Pakistanis, particularly those living abroad, to uphold Jinnah’s principles of “Unity, Faith and Discipline”.
The Independence Day ceremony began with the hoisting of the national flag to the strains of the national anthem, followed by the recitation of verses from the Holy Quran and the reading of messages from Pakistan’s president, prime minister and deputy prime minister.
In his address, Ambassador Sheikh used the occasion to underline Pakistan’s continuing importance to the US and the wider world.
His remarks echoed a message issued by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Pakistan’s Independence Day, in which he specifically referred to the two countries’ cooperation on regional mediation, along with critical minerals, energy, counterterrorism, cultural heritage, and trade and investment.
The reference to regional mediation is particularly significant given Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts involving Washington and Tehran. Islamabad has sought to use its relations with both sides to facilitate dialogue and help ease tensions between the United States and Iran.
The ceremony also included an investiture ceremony for Waqar Ali Khan, who received the President’s Award for Pride of Performance in recognition of his decades of service as a community leader and cultural ambassador in the US.

title: Govt opts for high-level talks as strike strains ports
description: Federal minister Aleem Khan, Sindh governor to meet goods transporters in Karachi; security authorities join efforts to help break deadlock.
author: Kalbe Ali
content:
• Federal minister Aleem Khan, Sindh governor to meet goods transporters in Karachi • Security authorities join efforts to help break deadlock
ISLAMABAD: With congestion beginning to build at the ports due to a pile-up of containers, the eight-day strike by truckers and edible oil tankers could end on Sunday (today) following a crucial round of talks at Governor House in Karachi between senior federal and provincial government officials and representatives of the transporters.
Sources in the federal government told Dawn that the prolonged disruption and its impact on trade had prompted official efforts to resolve the dispute, with security authorities also becoming involved in attempts to break the deadlock.
“The concerns of the striking truckers and edible oil tankers are genuine, but the government too has its procedural limitations,” a senior official said, adding that the transporters were seeking a strong guarantor regarding implementation of any agreement.
Communications Minister Abdul Aleem Khan, who was appointed by the prime minister as the focal person for negotiations with the transporters, and Punjab Transport Minister Bilal Akbar are scheduled to travel to Karachi to participate in the talks.
The Sindh governor, the provincial transport minister and other officials, including representatives of the Karachi Port Trust (KPT) and Port Qasim Authority, are also expected to attend.
A senior KPT official said the situation at the port was not yet critical, but congestion had become visible because of containers piling up amid the strike.
The goods transporters have been protesting for more than eight days under the banner of the All Pakistan Goods Transport Ittehad.
Officials said several categories of transporters had joined the strike and their demands involved different government departments, complicating negotiations.
One of the major sticking points is the seven per cent withholding tax on goods transport, which stood at 6pc in the previous fiscal year compared to 2pc for fuel tankers.
Striking truckers, container trailer operators and edible oil tanker operators are demanding that their withholding tax also be reduced to 2pc.
However, Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) sources said such a reduction could only be made through the Fin­­­ance Bill and could therefore be considered as part of the 2027-28 budget.
Another contentious issue is the Customs department’s practice of impounding vehicles found carrying smuggled or illicit goods.
“Regarding impounding of vehicles carrying smuggled or illicit goods, the point is why carriers book such items if they are not part of the smuggling network,” an official said.
Meanwhile, the government has decided to offer relief on some other demands, including establishment of a dedicated parking facility for trailers and trucks handling cargo at Karachi port.
The communications ministry has also agreed to provide temporary relief to 10-wheeler trucks regarding the upper axle-load limit on highways and motorways.
All Pakistan Goods Transport Itt­e­­had spokesman Muhammad Owais Chaudhry said the nationwide protest was continuing and thousands of vehicles remained off the roads.
“There was a brief round of talks with several authorities in Karachi today. We made it clear that our first priority is to find a sustainable solution to the issue through negotiations,” he said, accusing the bureaucracy of trying to create divisions among transporters.
“The main problem is that they have made mere verbal assurances, but that is not sufficient. How can we end the strike without practical progress on our demands?” he said.
He appealed to transporters to remain united and peaceful and avoid relying on rumours.
Asked about Sunday’s meeting, Mr Chaudhry said some guarantors were now becoming involved in efforts to resolve the dispute.

title: Mir Raza Ali murder case: Court directs investigators to complete probe until Aug 24
description: Additional evidence recovered from crime scene: investigation team.Court directs Ali's business partner to cooperate with investigators.Probe team retrieves digital devices from NCCIA, to be sent to PFSA.KARACHI: A judicial magistrate...
author: Amin Anwar
content:
Published August 15, 2026
KARACHI: A judicial magistrate on Saturday granted investigators until August 24 to complete the probe into the death of young businessman Mir Raza Ali after the investigating officer (IO) apprised the court that the inquiry had yet to be finalised.
Ali, an IBA graduate and businessman, was found dead in Gulistan-e-Jauhar a day after he went missing on July 28. His father has maintained that his son was murdered and rejected suggestions that his death was a case of suicide.
IO Siraj Lashari appeared before the East judicial magistrate and sought additional time to conclude the investigation and submit a report. The court accepted the request and directed investigators to present their findings at the next hearing on August 24.
Investigation officials said that the committee also retrieved Ali's mobile phone and smartwatch from the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA).
The devices will now be sent to the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) in Lahore for forensic examination.
According to officials, the move comes after Ali's family expressed reservations about having the devices examined by the NCCIA and sought an independent forensic analysis.
The officials added that additional evidence had been recovered from the crime scene; however, no further details were disclosed.
Investigators probing the death of the young businessman have expanded the inquiry committee, increasing the members from 7 to 9.
The newly inducted members include the SHO of Shah Latif Town police station and a deputy superintendent of police (DSP).
In a separate development, an additional district and sessions judge extended the pre-arrest bail of Ali's business partner, Muhammad Ahmed, until August 24.
During the hearing, Ahmed's counsel told the court that his client had been called to the crime scene at around 1am.
The lawyer argued that his client feared being implicated in the case despite assisting the inquiry. The court later restrained police from harassing him pending further proceedings.
After hearing arguments, the court extended the interim bail and directed Ahmed to cooperate with investigators and join the ongoing probe.
Speaking to reporters outside the court, Jibran Nasir, counsel for the deceased businessman's father, said the victim's family had provided investigators with the names of individuals who might possess information relevant to the case but had not accused anyone of involvement in the killing.
"The parents have not used the word 'suspect' for any individual," Nasir said, adding that names, including that of Ahmed, had been shared only to help investigators pursue all possible leads.
He described the case as a "blind murder" and said the family did not want to level allegations without evidence.
Nasir expressed confidence in the newly-constituted investigation team, saying its inquiry was not contradicting the available medical evidence and was being conducted in accordance with standard operating procedures (SOPs).
He said the family wanted investigators to ensure accurate geo-fencing analysis, obtain relevant CCTV footage and complete forensic examinations.
The lawyer also criticised the handling of the case by the previous investigation team, alleging that serious procedural lapses had occurred during the initial stages of the inquiry.
He claimed that a crime scene unit had failed to reach the site and alleged that the scene had been set on fire, potentially affecting the collection of DNA evidence.
"Our focus is on identifying the killers," he said, adding that the family wanted those responsible to be arrested alive and brought before the courts so the case could proceed through the legal process.

title: Forces eliminate 10 terrorists in Khuzdar operation
description: Several others injured as three hideouts targeted in Shor Pard; search underway for those who escaped.
author: Saleem Shahid
content:
• Several others injured as three hideouts targeted in Shor Pard • Search underway for those who escaped
QUETTA: Security forces killed 10 terrorists and injured many others in an intelligence-based operation in Shor Pard area of Khuzdar district on Saturday.
During the operation, security forces cordoned off and engaged multiple terrorist hideouts. Accor­ding to security sources, the terrorists were operating in three separate groups, leading to an intense exchange of fire with the security forces.
“As a result of the operation, 10 terrorists were killed, while several others sustained injuries,” security sources said.
They said that following the engagement, security forces launched an extensive search and clearance operation across the surrounding area. Efforts were underway to track down the terrorists who managed to escape.
Security forces have reaffirmed their determination to continue targeted operations against terrorist elements and to eliminate the threat of terrorism from the region. They pledged that the search operation would continue until all remaining terrorists were located and brought to justice.
Tribute paid to forces
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to security forces for the successful operation in the mountainous region of Shor Parod, state-run APP reported.
“Security forces killed 10 terrorists in a successful operation. Successful operations against terrorists who are enemies of humanity, are a manifestation of the expertise of our security forces,” he said in a statement.
“The entire nation is with the security forces in the war against terrorism. We are determined to completely eradicate terrorism from the country,” he added.
The development came a day after Balochistan Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langove survived an armed attack on his convoy while returning to Quetta after attending a flag-hoisting ceremony in Kalat.
Armed men hiding in the mountains targeted the convoy in the Kund Umrani area of Khad Kocha as it travelled along the Quetta-Karachi National Highway, injuring nine people, including seven police personnel deployed to protect the minister.
On Wednesday, the military’s media wing said eight terrorists were killed when explosive material detonated during the preparation of a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device in the Surab district of Balochistan.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations, security forces launched a comprehensive clearance operation following the explosion on Monday morning, tracking down and killing another 10 terrorists affiliated with Fitna Al Hindustan.
The initial explosion of explosive material also resulted in civilian casualties and ISPR said that at least three civilians lost their lives in a secondary detonation of other explosives stored at the terrorists’ hideout.
“In total, 18 terrorists affiliated with Fitna al-Hindustan have been eliminated so far,” the ISPR said, adding that two soldiers were injured during an exchange of fire.

title: President Zardari approves civil awards for 355 personalities from diverse fields
description: Journalists, artists and athletes feature among award recipients.Security personnel and martyrs to receive gallantry awards.Foreign dignitaries, overseas Pakistanis will also receive honours.President Asif Ali Zardari has approved...
author: Web Desk
content:
Published August 15, 2026
President Asif Ali Zardari has approved civil awards for 355 individuals in recognition of their contributions to a wide range of fields, including science, education, medicine, arts, sports and public service.
The list includes federal ministers, government officials, academics, doctors, journalists, artists, writers, athletes, philanthropists, security personnel, police officers, martyrs and foreign dignitaries, The News reported.
Ministers recommended for Nishan-i-Imtiaz: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Finance and Revenue Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Federal Minister for Establishment and Economic Affairs Ahad Khan Cheema and Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani, all of whom have been recommended for Nishan-i-Imtiaz, Hafiz Muhammad Tahir Mehmood Ashrafi — Tamgha-i-Imtiaz under the public service category.
The list further recommends Intelligence Bureau Director General Fuad Asadullah, Attorney General Mansoor Usman Awan, Finance Division Secretary Imdadullah Bosal, FBR Chairman Rashid Mahmood Lagrial and Establishment Division Secretary Nabeel A. Awan for Hilal-i-Imtiaz.
A large number of other serving and former public servants have also been recommended for Sitara-i-Imtiaz and Tamgha-i-Imtiaz, including officials from the finance, revenue, police, administration, commerce, law and other government sectors.
In the science category, Dr Shahid Mahmud, CEO/Chairman of Interactive Group of Companies, has been recommended for Hilal-i-Imtiaz.
Prof Dr Syed Zafar Ilyas and Prof Dr Mudassir Asrar have been proposed for Sitara-i-Imtiaz, while Dr Sajjad Hussain, Prof Dr Aneela Zameer Jaffery and Dr Urooj Saeed have been recommended for Tamgha-i-Imtiaz.
The engineering category includes Dr Muhammad Sadiq, Vice Chancellor of UET Peshawar, and Prof Dr Naeemul Haq Tariq, Principal Engineer/Professor at PIEAS, both recommended for Tamgha-i-Imtiaz.
Among educationists, Lt Gen (retd) Moazzam Ejaz, Rector of NUTECH, has been recommended for Hilal-i-Imtiaz. Prof Dr Muhammad Raza Shah, Prof Dr Khalid Masood Gondal, Dr Rashid Amjad and Dr Zafar Iqbal Qadir are among those proposed for Sitara-i-Imtiaz.
Several university vice chancellors, researchers, professors and education administrators have also been recommended for Tamgha-i-Imtiaz.
Doctors and healthcare professionals: Fifteen leading medical and health professionals, including Prof Dr Syed Jamal Raza and Prof Faisal Saud Dar and the late Prof Dr Tahir Shamsi and the late Dr Naseem Salahuddin, with civil awards for their outstanding services to medicine and healthcare, while DRAP Chief Executive Officer Dr Obaidullah has also been selected for Sitara-i-Imtiaz.
Artists and performers: The arts category features prominent names from film, television, theatre, music, painting and traditional arts.
Actor Balqees Bano, popularly known as Nisho Begum, comedian Iftikhar Ahmed Thakur, and Naat Khawan Syed Fasihuddin Soharwardhy are among those proposed for Sitara-i-Imtiaz.
The recommendations also include a large number of performers and artists proposed for PAPP, while several singers, actors, painters, musicians and traditional artisans have been recommended for Tamgha-i-Imtiaz.
Writers and poets: In literature, Asad Muhammad Khan has been recommended for the country’s highest civil award, Nishan-i-Imtiaz, for his contribution as a fiction and play writer and poet.
Poets Ejaz Rahim and Muhammad Khurshidul Hasan Rizvi have been proposed for Hilal-i-Imtiaz. Muhammad Shakeel Adilzada, Prof Brigadier (retd) Waheeduz-Zaman Tariq, Maqsood Hussain Jafri, Riazul Haq Tahir Riaz Majeed, Muhammad Hafeez Khan, Prof Dr Muhammad Saleem Mazhar, Hashim Nadeem and Syed Ghulam Abbas (Muhsin Naqvi) are among those recommended for Sitara-i-Imtiaz.
The journalism category includes Muhammad Saleh Zaafir and Haji Nawaz Raza, both recommended for Sitara-i-Imtiaz.
Syed Hammad Ghaznavi has been recommended for PAPP, while journalist and photographer Muhammad Amir Khan has also been proposed for PAPP.
Muhammad Riaz Khan, Shoaib Ahmed and M Ammar Masood have been recommended for Tamgha-i-Imtiaz.
News anchors Dr Maria Zulfiqar, Adil Shahzaib, Hammad Hassan and Tasawwar Arafat have also been recommended for Tamgha-i-Imtiaz.
Sports personalities: The sports category includes senior boxing coach Atta Mohammad Kakar and martial artist and yoga pioneer Dr Waseem A. Tai, both recommended for Sitara-i-Imtiaz.
Wrestler Bashir Bhola, shooter Kishmala Talat, squash player Noor Zaman, boxer Muhammad Waseem and cricketer Sadiq Muhammad are among those proposed for PAPP, while athlete Faiqa Riaz has been recommended for Tamgha-i-Imtiaz.
A substantial portion of the recommendations relates to gallantry and public service.
Dozens of personnel of the Federal Constabulary have been recommended posthumously for Sitara-i-Shujaat, including Nazakat Ali, Sepoy Muhammad Usman, Sepoy Mina Badshah, Sepoy Ibrar Ali, Sepoy Noorul Hasan, Sepoy Taza Gul, Lance Naik Muhammad Nazif and several others.
The list continues with police personnel, Intelligence Bureau officials and civilians recommended for Sitara-i-Shujaat. Among the nominees are HC Mumtaz Ahmad, Muhammad Yousaf Reki, Muhammad Afzal, Hidayatullah Bulaidi, Police Constable Muhammad Khumari, SHO Lutuf Ali Khosa and Group Captain Asim Tariq, all listed for posthumous awards.
Senior officers involved in security and law-enforcement operations have also been recommended for Sitara-i-Imtiaz, including IGP Abdul Kareem, DIG Waqas Hassan and DIG Tanveer Hussain Tunio in recognition of their gallantry/public service.
Several personnel have further been proposed for Tamgha-i-Shujaat and Tamgha-i-Imtiaz under gallantry/public service, including police officers and personnel of the Intelligence Bureau and military intelligence.
Under Services to Pakistan (Foreign Nationals), Her Highness Sheikha Fatima bint Mubarak has been recommended for Nishan-i-Pakistan.
The list also proposes Nishan-i-Quaid-i-Azam posthumously for physicians Dr Jal Rattanji Patel and Dr Jal Daeboo physicians of Quaid-i-Azam.
Several Saudi, Turkish, Russian, Japanese, Chinese and other foreign personalities have been recommended for Hilal-i-Pakistan, Hilal-i-Imtiaz, Sitara-i-Pakistan and Sitara-i-Quaid-i-Azam.
Among them are Prince Saud bin Nayef bin Abdulaziz Al-Saud, Saudi Education Minister Yousef bin Abdullah Al-Benyan, Mohammed Al-Tuwaijri, Deemah Al Yahya, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexey Logvinovich Overchuk, Japanese scholar Hiroji Kataoka and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan.
The recommendations also recognise overseas Pakistanis for their services to Pakistan.
Muhammad Asad, listed as an Austro-Hungarian Pakistani Muslim, has been recommended posthumously for Nishan-i-Imtiaz, while Dr Ghulam Murtaza, Prof Ahmed Ali and Sardar Muhammad Ilyas Khan have been proposed for Hilal-i-Imtiaz.
Several overseas Pakistanis based in the UAE, Japan, South Korea, the UK, the US, Saudi Arabia, Italy and other countries have been recommended for Sitara-i-Imtiaz and Tamgha-i-Imtiaz.

title: Pakistan says Islamabad MoU 'only way forward' amid US-Iran tensions
description: DPM Dar stresses dialogue, diplomacy for lasting regional peace.US envoy appreciates Pakistan's role in promoting stability.Dar, UK envoy discuss regional developments and cooperation.ISLAMABAD: Pakistan has renewed its call for...
author: Mariana Baabar
content:
Published August 15, 2026
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan has renewed its call for full implementation of the June 18 Islamabad memorandum of understanding, telling Washington that the agreement offered the "only way forward" towards regional peace and stability.
The same message was also conveyed to the United Kingdom. Though Friday was a national holiday as the nation celebrated its 79 years of independence, the office of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar remained open and US Charge d'Affaires Natalie A Baker called on him on Friday, The News reported on Saturday.
Pakistan's message to Washington comes at a time when Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatened Iran with economic isolation "like the world has never seen before", saying new measures are expected next week. It will be a combination of economic isolation like the world has never seen before.
The foreign minister appreciated the positive trajectory in Pakistan-US relations and underscored the importance of dialogue and diplomacy for lasting peace. "He stressed that the implementation of the Islamabad MoU of 18 June in letter and spirit is the only way forward," the Foreign Office said in a statement. Dar also reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to regional peace and security while safeguarding its national interests.
"Discussions centred on Pakistan-US bilateral cooperation and recent regional developments. The US Chargé appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability and conveyed felicitations to the DPM/FM on Pakistan's Independence Day," added the statement.
Meanwhile, the meeting between Baker and Dar was followed by UK High Commissioner to Pakistan Jane Marriott calling on the foreign minister. "Recent regional and international developments also figured in the discussion. DPM/FM stressed that the Islamabad MoU should be implemented by the parties in letter and spirit and reaffirmed that dialogue and diplomacy remain the only way forward to address outstanding issues," said the FO.
Dar appreciated the positive momentum in Pakistan-UK relations while also recalling his recent meeting with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband on the sidelines of the ASEAN Regional Forum in Manila and highlighted the importance of sustained high-level contacts. They discussed key areas of mutual interest and ways to further strengthen bilateral cooperation.
Ambassador of China Jiang Zaidong also called on the foreign minister, who conveyed condolences on the tragic death of a Chinese mountaineer following an avalanche incident at Broad Peak in Gilgit-Baltistan and promised full facilitation for the return of the deceased’s remains. Ambassador Jiang Zaidong appreciated Pakistan’s prompt assistance and support following the incident.
"Views were also exchanged on regional developments and other matters of mutual interest while Ambassador Jiang Zaidong extended warm congratulations to the people and leadership of Pakistan on the occasion of Independence Day, reaffirming the close and time-tested ties between the two countries," said the statement.
Earlier, the foreign minister spoke on the telephone with his Egyptian counterpart Badr Abdelatty, who extended warm greetings on Pakistan’s Independence Day to the leadership, government and people of Pakistan, and conveyed his best wishes for continued peace, progress and prosperity.
"The two leaders reaffirmed the close and brotherly relations between Pakistan and Egypt and expressed their shared commitment to further strengthening cooperation across all areas of mutual interest, including through enhanced high-level exchanges and close institutional engagement.
"They also exchanged views on regional and international developments of mutual interest and agreed to remain in close contact," said the Foreign Office.

title: The influencers getting bitten chasing the perfect shark shot
description: Tayane Dalazen was on a shark-diving trip in Brazil when she was attacked.
author: Will Vernon
content:
A nurse shark bit Tayane Dalazen while she was diving off the Brazilian coast
"I knew something was different because the sharks were on the surface," says Tayane Dalazen, a 37-year old Brazilian lawyer and social media personality.
"There were a lot of them," she says. "Later, I discovered [the tour organisers] were feeding the sharks so that they would interact with the tourists."
Dalazen, from Sao Paulo, was on a shark-diving trip on the Brazilian coast in April when she suddenly felt "strong pressure" on her leg.
"When the shark bit me, the pain was very strong," she says. "I stayed calm because I knew I couldn't fight the animal."
A nurse shark, more than seven feet (two metres) long, had clamped its jaws around her thigh.
After holding her underwater for several seconds, the shark released her and she was able to escape. But Dalazen says the experience, which left her with lacerations to her thigh, was "very frightening".
Dalazen posted footage of the shark bite online, where it's since been viewed tens of millions of times. Although she says she "wasn't there for social media" and didn't touch or provoke the shark, she admits she was too close to the animals.
Incidents of sharks biting humans are incredibly rare, but at least three influencers have been bitten by the animals in less than a year. Scientists say they're increasingly concerned about the rise in social media videos showing people swimming too close to sharks, touching or even riding them.
"I'm seeing these videos every single week now and it's way more than it ever used to be," says shark scientist Kristian Parton, who also hosts the 'Shark Bytes' YouTube channel. "We're going to see people ending up in really serious incidents with sharks."
In July, a fishing influencer almost lost his leg after being attacked by a reef shark whilst spearfishing. In December, a Chinese content creator was bitten in the Maldives. Both incidents were caught on camera.
Researchers at the International Shark Attack File, which tracks human-shark interactions worldwide, have also told the BBC they've seen a marked increase in the past three years of people being bitten while trying to take footage with sharks.
A recent study of "swim with wildlife" expeditions , external found influencers and photographers were the most likely to ignore safety instructions.
In February last year, a tourist in the Caribbean had both hands bitten off while trying to get a photograph of a bull shark from the shallows, according to local authorities. Two months later, a snorkeller in Israel carrying a "selfie stick" was killed by sharks, reportedly while trying to get photographs .
The risk of being bitten by a shark remains extremely low: the number of unprovoked shark attacks worldwide has remained broadly stable for the past 30 years, at about 70 bites per year.
While Tayane Dalazen was bitten by a nurse shark - known as a more docile species - some influencers have been filmed touching tiger sharks and even great whites.
"We're talking about a true apex predator, a very large wild animal," says Parton. "You wouldn't walk into the Serengeti and try and put your hand on the face of a lion."
Sharks will often use defensive or "exploratory" bites when presented by an unwelcome human in their personal space, he adds.
Human interactions can also cause stress to the animals. Scientific studies have shown that approaching or touching a shark leads to high levels of hormones called glucocorticoids. These can lead to a weakened immune system, increased mortality and aborted offspring.
"If you're approaching the shark and stressing it out, whether it be in a nursery habitat, a breeding ground, or a feeding area, you're depriving that shark of an area that's important to it to survive," explains Parton, "and that's definitely a problem."
One of the best-known shark content creators is Ocean Ramsey, a 38-year-old former model who shot to fame in 2019 after she was pictured swimming with one of the largest great white sharks ever seen.
Divers take plunge with great white shark
She often posts footage of her touching sharks and holding their dorsal fins.
She spoke to the BBC from a boat in Hawaii, where she runs "Dive with Ocean" shark tours for paying customers.
"My intent with all of my content has never been to gain views, it's to gain protection for sharks," Ramsey says. "I've contributed to research articles, data collection... all of my work stems down to education."
She denies that getting close to the sharks and touching them causes harm: "Most of my work and what I share is respecting and observing from a distance," she says.
"I observe their behaviour and they choose to interact with me. They always make the first approach."
What about claims by scientists that videos showing sharks being touched encourage others to take risks and do the same?
"You've got to give the general public some accountability," Ramsey insists. "I think most people are observing what I'm sharing with an educational message and they're not going out to just replicate that."
Ocean Ramsey says her intent has "never been to gain views"
The BBC spoke to several content creators who all denied being motivated by social media views, clicks or revenue, and insisted they were supporting conservation or attempting to change public perceptions of sharks.
Shark expert Dr Jack Cooper describes those claims as "ludicrous".
"I really cannot explain how going up to a shark and touching it or riding it is doing anything to aid conservation," he says. "All you're doing is showing a shark getting harassed by a human. And that's not promoting any policies about what we could do to reduce overfishing or to give more protections for sharks.
"And it's certainly not providing scientific data that will tell us how the shark populations are doing or what policies might actually help conserve them."
A number of videos on social media show people touching sharks
Eric Clua, a marine biologist at the Ãcole Pratique des Hautes Ãtudes in Paris, who has done research into the motivations behind shark bites, says the number of incidents caused by people getting too close to sharks is increasing, as a consequence of people considering sharks less dangerous than before.
"The message transmitted by influencers is 'Look! Touch the shark, nothing will happen to you,'" he says.
Shark swimming and diving are booming in popularity around the world. Travel site TripAdvisor currently lists more than 140 such experiences in the Maldives alone. Some of the listings advertise "the ultimate selfie" with sharks.
But the warning from experts is clear: getting that perfect shot could come at a painful price.

title: Chart-topping game No 10: Full Confidence puts you in prime minister's shoes
description: Mobile game No 10: Full Confidence recently ranked above Minecraft on the UK App Store paid games chart
author: Laura Cress
content:
Players in the prime minister simulator No 10: Full Confidence must balance the moods of factions including their cabinet and the media
A mobile game made by a developer in Manchester has recently beaten the global phenomenon Minecraft to top Apple's paid games chart.
Its success is perhaps even more surprising given its subject matter - UK politics.
No 10: Full Confidence by Benjamin Brewis sees players take on the role of prime minister, making decisions through a wave of parliamentary scenarios and trying to remain in power for as long as possible.
The success of Brewis's app, and the creation of others like it, suggests the dramatic recent ebb and flow of Westminster may have inspired a popular new sub-genre.
This video can not be played
No 10: Full Confidence is a prime minister simulator game
In No 10: Full Confidence , external , players who take on the precarious position of prime minister must balance the moods of four factions - their cabinet, backbenchers, the media, and the public - to remain in the game. Decisions are made across more than 300 fictional political scenarios, handwritten by Brewis.
The storylines range from the mundane - dealing with GP appointment waiting times - to the absurd.
"I have a two or three-part storyline where a dog is let loose into the House of Lords by a lobbyist during a vet bill and that spirals out of control," Brewis said.
Each scenario asks players to pick one action from three choices on the screen, with each potentially upsetting or pleasing the different factions.
Much like in real life, if one side completely turns against you your political career is finished.
While some situations may sound farcical, Brewis said he had plenty of real life examples to draw on as inspiration.
"I'd remember that MP who had a spider that he'd threaten MPs with , or when Boris Johnson walked into a fridge. I'm frantically writing them all down."
My first attempt at playing prime minister in No 10: Full Confidence hasn't left me considering a Westminster career.
As my chosen candidate, Verity Grimshaw, I start off strong, managing to survive a crisis in which thousands of A-level students receive the wrong grades.
I only manage to stay in the post for one year and nine months, taken out - somewhat ironically given my actual job - by a complete lack of trust by the press.
Unfortunately, a cabinet minister resigns and publishes a three-page-long letter that contains the phrase "the PM was warned" four times.
This letter being read out in full on BBC Radio 4 turns out to be the last straw for poor Verity.
My final choice in the game of "respond directly, address every point, don't let it sit unanswered", seemingly does not go down very well.
Brewis says some users have fared a lot better than my sorry effort.
"Someone has stayed in for 1,885 months, which is 157 years," he says. "I'm not sure if that's a democracy any more."
One scenario players must navigate in No 10: Full Confidence raises big questions about livestock
Brewis said he was inspired to begin creating the app around December 2025, when "it was all kicking off" with former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer, and talk of potential challenges to his leadership was starting to grow.
"I remember thinking at the time, someone should just start taking the mick out of this," he said. "We've had so many prime ministers - it's funny now."
Five different people have occupied No 10 since 2016 - three in the space of just over three years, and one for just 49 days.
Dr Russell Foster, a lecturer in British and International Politics at King's College London, said the "churn of prime ministers" and growing presence of politics on social media could also help explain why Westminster is suddenly appearing on our devices.
And it was all going so well...
No 10: Full Confidence is not the only game based around Westminster's wheeling and dealing.
Fantasy Parliament , external is a browser-based game designed by another UK-based developer, Evan Roberts, which lets players draft their own fantasy league of real-world MPs, scoring points based on their real-life media coverage.
With the strategy game's Policy Tester, players can even type in proposals to a ChatGPT-style AI model, which then replies in the style of how it believes different groups of voters - such as Coastal Keith or Graduate Gemma - would react.
Meanwhile, UK Politics Simulator, "built on real UK data down to ward level", is reportedly due out later this year for PC, made by the Scarborough-based company Black Cannon Games.
Despite the success of his own venture, currently ranking 5th in Apple's UK paid games charts - above Monopoly Go - Brewis said he does not know if any politicians have actually played his game.
However, he has received some feedback on how accurately the game depicts UK political life, from his friends who work in the civil service.
"It's exactly like this," they told him, "but worse."

title: Police recover Indonesian woman in Hyderabad, hand her over to consulate
description: Police detain husband Naik Mohammad; woman alleges she was being subjected to domestic violence.
author: The Newspaper's Staff Correspondent
content:
HYDERABAD: An Indonesian woman, Indah Marlyan, was recovered under judicial orders and handed over to her country’s consulate by the district police on Saturday.
The woman had married a man, Naik Mohammad Shaikh alias Mohammad Hamza Mirza. She had submitted a complaint to the consulate alleging that she was being subjected to domestic violence.
The consulate took up the matter with Sindh government functionaries and an application was filed through the women development department before the additional district judge-V under Section 491 Cr.PC for her recovery.
SSP Hyderabad Shahzeb Chachar told Dawn on Saturday that the woman, along with her infant baby girl, was handed over to the Indonesian consulate under judicial supervision.
The police have detained Naik Mohammad.
The action was taken by police after the women development department through its employee, Ishtiaq Channa, filed the application in the court for her recovery.
The applicant said that the woman was held in wrongful confinement by Naik Mohammad Shaikh, a resident of Gul Latif Housing Society in Qasimabad. He said that the department had received an application on Aug 8 for protection. He said the woman alleged that she was being threatened and assaulted by her husband. He sought a court order in this regard.
The woman had also approached her country’s consulate in Karachi for help. The consulate, according to official sources, had taken up the matter with the Sindh chief secretary and IGP for her safe recovery.
The court ordered the SSP SHO concerned to recover the woman and produce her in the court on Aug 13, which was complied with.

title: UK assures Pakistan of swift action on students’ visa delays
description: Stresses the need to remove obstacles faced by Pakistani students seeking education abroad and facilitate them.
author: Kashif Abbasi
content:
ISLAMABAD: The federal law and justice minister raised the issue of delays in UK visas for Pakistani students while the British high commissioner assured resolution of the issue.
British High Commissioner Jane Marriott called on Federal Minister for Law & Justice Senator Azam Nazeer Tarar. The meeting discussed Pakistan-UK bilateral relations, matters of mutual interest and ways to further strengthen cooperation between the two countries, says a press release issued here.
It said that during the meeting, the minister raised the issue of delays in UK visas for Pakistani students and conveyed the government’s concern to the British High Commissioner.
The law minister said that hundreds of Pakistani students were facing difficulties due to delays in visa processing, with a risk that the delays could result in the loss of their academic year.
He stressed the need to remove obstacles faced by Pakistani students seeking education abroad and facilitate them in this regard. The minister briefed the British high commissioner that, on the directives of the prime minister, a committee under his chairmanship was working to improve the legal and institutional framework concerning Pakistani students studying abroad.
He further informed the high commissioner that, on the prime minister’s directives, the committee had finalised its recommendations on the matter, and work was underway to further improve the legal and institutional framework for Pakistani students pursuing education abroad.
The minister said that the legal and institutional framework for Pakistani students seeking education abroad was being improved to develop an effective mechanism for addressing the issues faced by students.
Ms Marriott assured the Federal Minister that the issue of delays in visas for Pakistani students would be addressed. The meeting also discussed further strengthening educational linkages between Pakistan and the United Kingdom, as well as enhancing institutional cooperation and engagement between the two countries.
The press release said that Minister of State for Law, Justice and Human Rights Barrister Aqeel Malik was also present during the meeting.

title: Police questioning Mir Raza Ali's 35 phone contacts: IO
description: DSP Lashari tells court no one named as suspect yet; murder probe still underway.
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
content:
KARACHI: Investigators probing the Mir Raza Ali murder case are questioning as many as 35 persons who were found to have been in contact with the deceased over the phone.
The information was provided by the newly appointed investigating officer (IO), DSP Siraj Lashari, to a judicial magistrate on Saturday.
Young businessman and IBA graduate Mir Raza had gone missing on July 28 and his bullet-riddled body was found a day later in bushes in Gulistan-i-Jauhar.
On Saturday, DSP Lashari appeared in court and sought more time to file a progress report as he took over the case just two days ago.
DSP Lashari tells court no one named as accused yet; murder probe still underway
He stated that around 35 suspects were being interrogated as the call data record reflected that they were in contact with the victim.
He submitted that the police have yet to name anyone as accused since the investigation was still underway and more time was needed to conclude it.
He sought more time to complete the investigation as well as to collect forensic and medical reports.
The court granted him time to conclude the investigation and asked him to file a progress report on Aug 24.
Business partner’s bail extended
Also on Saturday, a sessions court extended the interim pre-arrest bail of Mir Raza’s business partner Muhammad Ahmed Bhardey till Aug 24.
An additional district and sessions judge (East) had granted pre-arrest bail to the applicant against a surety of Rs100,000 till Aug 15.
On Saturday, applicant’s counsel Khalid Mumtaz submitted that his client was being harassed by police and he might be arrested despite extending full cooperation with investigators.
He informed the court that the applicant had been summoned to the crime scene rather than to a police station.
Representing the deceased’s family, Advocate Jibran Nasir submitted that the police had merely summoned the applicant, along with around 35 others, for the investigation process.
The judge questioned why the applicant had sought bail when he had not initially been named as an accused in the case.
The court also made it clear that the applicant would have to join the investigation regardless of whether he remained on bail.
The applicant informed the court that he had been appearing at the police station whenever the police called him.
The judge directed him not to leave the city while the investigation was underway and extended his interim bail until Aug 24.

title: Unofficial results: PPP, PML-N bag one seat each from AJK's Bagh district
description: Voting took place at nine stations in LA-15, 14 in LA-16.Elections at the polling station had been postponed on Aug 10.PML-N and PPP have won 24 and 11 seats, respectively, so far.The Pakistan Peoples Party and Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz ...
author: Web Desk
content:
Published August 15, 2026
The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) have clinched one seat each in Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s (AJK) Bagh district, show unofficial results.
According to unverified and unofficial results from all 186 polling stations in LA-16, PML-N candidate Mir Akbar Khan won the seat by securing 20,793 votes, followed by PPP’s Qamar Zaman Khan, who received 16,964 votes.
In LA-15 Bagh-II, PPP’s Zia Qamar emerged victorious with 17,019 votes, while his closest contender, PML-N’s Mushtaq Minhas, secured 15,127 votes.
Balloting began at 8am and continued uninterrupted until 5pm. People exercised their democratic right at nine polling stations in LA-15 Bagh-2 and 14 stations in LA-16 Bagh-3 today.
The election had been postponed at the stations on August 10 after polling staff failed to arrive amid tensions.
The AJK Election Commission had decided to hold Legislative Assembly elections for 45 seats, including 12 refugee seats, in three phases.
In the first phase, elections were held across 13 constituencies in Mirpur Division. The second phase of the AJK elections took place on August 2, with polling held in eight constituencies of Muzaffarabad Division and all 12 refugee constituencies amid rigging allegations.
The electoral process in LA-27 (Muzaffarabad-I) and LA-27 was postponed due to heavy rain and landslides.
The PML-N emerged as the dominant party in AJK following the first two phases of the region's elections.
With the latest results, PML-N’s tally has risen to 25 seats, while PPP has secured 11.
Polling for the third phase of the AJK elections was held in four constituencies across Bagh and Haveli districts of Poonch division on August 10.
According to the AJK Election Commission, Awami Dast-o-Baazo party's  Sajid Iqbal Abbasi won the elections from LA-14 Bagh-I. PPP leader and AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore remained successful on LA-17 Bagh IV, defeating PML-N’s Mohsin Aziz.
The AJK election commission withheld results of LA-16 Bagh-III and LA-15 Bagh-II as polling could not be held at some of the polling stations on August 10.

title: Mir Raza Ali's father seeks suspension of East DIG, others for 'concealing evidence'
description: Mir Hussain seeks suspenion of Ferozabad SHO. Says police officers “played a game” with him. Ali's family sought analysis of his smartwatch at PFSA.Mir Hussain Ali, the father of slain 25-year-old...
author: Web Desk
content:
Published August 14, 2026
Mir Hussain Ali, the father of slain 25-year-old businessman Mir Raza Ali, on Friday demanded that Karachi East Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Dr Farrukh Ali and others be suspended for allegedly delaying the investigation and attempting to conceal evidence.
Talking to journalists, Mir Hussain urged the authorities to also suspend the Ferozabad station house officer for his alleged role in mishandling the murder case of his son.
He said that the police officers “played a game” with the bereaved family.
Ali, an IBA graduate and businessman, was found dead in Gulistan-e-Jauhar a day after he went missing on July 28.
Initially, police were working on the possibility that he had died by suicide; however, his father maintained that his son had been kidnapped, tortured and killed.
A day earlier, the family of the deceased businessman opposed the forensic examination of his smartwatch by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) as their lawyer Jibran Nasir had sought analysis of the device at the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA).
Speaking to Geo News, Nasir had said the smartwatch had remained in the possession of the former committee head for several days before being handed over to the NCCIA on Wednesday.
The lawyer had said the family did not want the smartwatch examined by the NCCIA and instead wanted it forensically analysed at the PFSA, a Lahore-based facility operating under the Punjab Home Department.
Nasir had also raised concerns about possible tampering, citing the fact that the smartwatch had remained with the former committee head for several days.
The new investigation committee held its meeting at Ferozabad police station on Thursday, according to investigation sources. Several key decisions regarding the investigation were made during the meeting, and committee members were assigned specific responsibilities, the sources  had added.
Following the meeting, committee members proceeded to the incident site to collect additional evidence as part of the ongoing investigation. The sources had said the previous investigating officer also accompanied the team to assist with the inquiry.
The committee chief, DIG Karachi Branch, was briefed on the investigation. This marked the DIG's first visit to the incident site since assuming leadership of the committee.
Committee members also interviewed the nursery staff and gathered further details relevant to the case, according to investigation sources.
Meanwhile, the new investigation team, headed by Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Amir Farooqi, had written four separate letters to the NCCIA, according to investigation sources.
The team had requested a forensic examination of the deceased businessman's smartwatch, according to the contents of the letters.
It had also sought details of Ali's social media accounts and other digital accounts, the sources said.
The new investigation team would hold its second meeting at Ferozabad police station, sources had said. Following the meeting, the team would revisit the crime scene as part of its ongoing investigation.

Published August 14, 2026
President Asif Ali Zardari on Friday appreciated the efforts of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, and Field Marshal and Chief of Defence Forces, Syed Asim Munir for transforming the longstanding fraternal ties among Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan into a stronger strategic partnership.
PM Shehbaz called on the president at the Aiwan-e-Sadr and felicitated him on the occasion of Independence Day, a statement said. The prime minister briefed the president on the "historic" Makkah Joint Defence Agreement reached among Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan on August 7.
Under the agreement signed during the Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence, an armed attack against any one of the three countries would be regarded as an attack against them all.
The president expressed his best wishes for effective implementation of the trilateral peace agreement, particularly in promoting defence cooperation, regional peace and stability and the security of the Muslim Ummah.
In the meeting, appreciation was expressed for the professional capabilities of Pakistan's armed forces and law enforcement agencies in operations against the terrorists of Fitna al-Hindustan and Fitna al-Khawarij, including internal and external affairs, the President's Office said.
The resolve was also reiterated to completely eradicate the scourge of terrorism from the beloved homeland.
The statement added that the president emphasised the need for effective measures to provide relief to the people amid the economic difficulties they face in the context of the current regional situation, and to ensure the uninterrupted supply of essential commodities and their availability at reasonable prices.
President Zardari hoped that Pakistan's effective diplomatic efforts for the promotion of regional and global peace would further strengthen the country's international standing, and that its positive impacts would be reflected in the national economy and the lives of the people.

title: Australia v Bangladesh: Mehidy Hasan Miraz inspires visitors to historic first Test win in Australia
description: Bangladesh thrash Australia by nine wickets on the fourth day of the series-opener in Darwin to complete one of Test cricket's greatest upsets.
author: Paul Battison
content:
Hasan Mahmud (right) was named player of the match after taking nine wickets in the opening Test
First Test, Darwin (day four of five)
Australia 198: (Smith 71; Mahmud 6-55) & 284 (Green 104; Miraz 5-66)
Bangladesh 426: (Tanzid 101, Shanto 84, Miraz 65; Hazlewood 6-89) & 57-1 (Mominul 30*)
Bangladesh win by nine wickets
Bangladesh thrashed Australia by nine wickets on the fourth day of the series-opener in Darwin to complete one of Test cricket's greatest upsets.
After bowling the hosts out for 284 and needing 57 to win, Mominul Haque cut Beau Webster to the boundary for the winning runs to seal the nation's first Test victory in Australia.
The moment sparked jubilation among Bangladesh players and staff as they celebrated arguably their greatest victory in 26 years of competing in Test cricket.
Australia are the top-ranked Test nation while Bangladesh haven't played a series under the five-day format in the country since a 2-0 defeat in 2003.
The visitors were on top of the match throughout, but it was spinner Mehidy Hasan Miraz who took the spotlight on day four as he took 5-66 to dismiss Australia for 284, leaving just 57 runs needed to win.
All-rounder Cameron Green showed fight with a valiant 104 but after being bowled by Hasan Mahmud, Australia's faint hopes of saving the Test all but disappeared.
Seamer Mahmud was named player of the match after claiming 6-55 in the first innings and 3-56 in the second.
"This is the biggest win so far for Bangladesh in any format," captain Najmul Hossain Shanto said.
"Going forward we want to do something special in the future. I'm very happy, proud of myself and the way the boys played. We did a lot of hard work."
Speaking on ABC, commentator Jim Maxwell described the result as one of the most "embarrassing defeats that Australia have ever suffered in Test cricket".
History for Bangladesh as they beat Australia in Darwin
Miraz's second innings performance followed a gritty 65 with the bat on day three that helped Bangladesh into a healthy first innings lead, before he dismissed talisman Steve Smith in Australia's second innings to set up victory.
The spinner continued his form on day four as he had wicketkeeper Alex Carey caught behind for 30 before bowling all-rounder Webster for five with a pair of sumptuous deliveries to bring Australia's tail into play.
The 28-year-old then had Australia captain Pat Cummins caught in close for eight, before a defiant 43-run eighth-wicket partnership between Green and Mitchell Starc was ended when Taskin Ahmed had the latter caught behind for 18.
Green dug in for his third Test century in his home country in a timely knock amid criticism of his place in the side, but after being dismissed by Mahmud, Miraz removed Nathan Lyon to leave Bangladesh in touching distance of victory.
Despite losing opener Tanzid Hasan Tamim for a duck to Josh Hazlewood in the second over, Mominul's unbeaten 30 and Shadman Islam's 25 sealed the resounding win.
"They outplayed us in all facets, they were patient and disciplined," said Cummins.
"I thought our prep was spot-on, no excuses."
Australia's only previous Test defeat by Bangladesh was at Mirpur in 2017.
The match was the first of a two-Test series, with the second beginning on 22 August (01:00 BST), which you can follow with live commentary on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra.
Australia v Bangladesh
Live ball-by-ball commentary on BBC Sounds, BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra from 00:30 BST each day (UK users only)
The result was all the more remarkable as Bangladesh, who are the ninth-ranked Test team, had been bowled out for just 54 by a Cricket Australia XI in a warm-up match in Darwin days earlier.
In June, they were thrashed by Zimbabwe, the lowest of cricket's 10-ranked Test-playing nations, in a one-off match in Harare.
Bangladesh's prime minister Tarique Rahman congratulated the team on a video call with the players.
"We're all eagerly waiting to welcome you home," he said on social media.
Bangladesh also went into the match against a full-strength Australian team with two of their leading fast bowlers, Nahid Rana and Shoriful Islam, out injured.
Shanto said the remarkable victory was helped by a mindset shift among his side's pacemen.
"Five years ago, pacers didn't want to play Tests," said Shanto.
"But we've been playing lots of Test cricket and they are giving importance to Test format. They want to play, want to perform, want to be world class. That is the mindset they now have.
"Seniors like Mushfiqur [Rahim] and Mominul [Haque] have encouraged them to play more Test cricket."

title: Leavitt and Ocasio-Cortez spark conversation on challenges of family and career
description: The White House press secretary quit this week to be with her children, while Democrat Alexandra Ocasio-Cortez said she was freezing her eggs.
author: Madeline Halpert
content:
White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt and Congresswoman Alexandra Ocasio-Cortez have both spoken in recent days about balancing their careers with motherhood
Last summer, Representative Sara Jacobs would run up to her office to give herself injections of hormones before rushing back to Congress for a session with her fellow lawmakers.
The shots were for the second round of freezing her eggs, a medical procedure that can give women more time to have children.
"It was an empowering decision that gave me more agency," the 37-year-old said, adding that the process was challenging.
"Your body hurts. Your hormones are crazy. It's kind of like puberty and menopause at the same time."
Jacobs announced she was beginning the egg freezing process in 2021, at a time when she said few lawmakers were discussing the topic in the halls of Congress.
The process - which can cost more than $10,000 (Â£7,400) and is rarely covered by insurance - involves doctors harvesting eggs from the ovaries and freezing them for a future pregnancy.
This week, Democratic Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez announced she too was beginning the process of freezing her eggs , documenting the daily mechanics of giving herself hormone shots on social media.
This video can not be played
Watch: Key moments from Karoline Leavitt's White House tenure
The left-wing Democrat's announcement sparked a conversation about the challenges of balancing motherhood and a demanding career, the same week that White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt announced she would be leaving the Trump administration to spend more time with her family, including her infant.
"The truth is since returning to the White House after the birth of my daughter, I have felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy and attention required of [being] the White House press secretary," Leavitt said.
Leavitt brought her son Nicholas, or "Niko", into the White House press briefing room during Thanksgiving last year
Several women with busy careers spoke to the BBC about the challenges of juggling their work with motherhood in the only industrialised nation that does not mandate paid parental leave.
Less than a quarter of workers in the US have access to paid family leave through their employer, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. More than 120 nations around the world - including all European countries - provide paid maternity leave.
In the US, women are increasingly having children at older ages, while more are choosing not to have children at all. From 2016 to 2023, the average age of all mothers giving birth in the US rose from 28.7 to 29.6, according to a 2025 report from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
Michele Heisler (left) says raising her children while working as a professor of medicine meant long nights, and lots of help
Michele Heisler, a professor of internal medicine at the University of Michigan, gave birth to her first child after going back to medical school at the age of 30. She was pregnant with her son during her third year of medical school.
Heisler, who serves as medical director for non-profit Physicians for Human Rights, said she had only been able to dedicate enough time to her career because of access to resources - including nannies - and a husband who was an equal partner in parenting.
"Unless it's clear that both are equal parents, [child rearing] is always going to fall on the woman, and then you're going to have to take a step back in some way," Heisler said.
Heisler said a flexible schedule is what allowed her to pursue her career to the fullest - staying up late at night to work and waking up sometimes at 05:00 to get her research done - so she could spend time with her children.
Legal scholar Seema Patel says she stays up late to finish work after her children are in bed
Seema Patel, an associate professor of law at UC Law San Francisco, also stays up late at night to try to finish her work so she doesn't have to miss moments with her children.
"The reality is that these years in your kids' lives are so fleeting, and I'm super aware of the time," she said.
Patel worked for San Francisco's Office of Labor Standards Enforcement, which became the first local government in the US to pass a law requiring employers to provide paid parental leave.
But through her career as a workers' rights lawyer, she has seen many lower-wage workers and parents who are not lucky enough to have access to paid time off.
When Patel began working as a federal attorney, her boss advised her to save up her vacation days in case she eventually wanted to have children and needed to take leave. She ended up taking the advice.
"I was a brand new, young attorney who had not even contemplated that stage of my life, but I had to in that moment, face that question of - I better be saving my vacation days," she said.
But even with some maternity leave and a dedicated partner, as her children - now ages 13, 11 and seven - have grown older, the work-life juggling act remains a challenge.
"I have a high-producing job," she said. "How can I do that while also being there for my kids and attentive to them? I don't have an answer."
Congresswoman Sara Jacobs documented her journey freezing her eggs on social media
For now, Jacobs, who has completed two rounds of egg freezing, plans to hold off on having children while her job requires her to fly across the country from California to Washington.
"Figuring out how to be a mum when I'm gone half the time across the country, it's logistically complicated," she said.
Jacobs said she was impressed by her fellow lawmakers who have managed to make it work. Only a handful of women have given birth while in Congress, while a few dozen lawmakers are mothers to children under the age of 18.
The federal government, like many US employers, does not offer paid parental leave, Jacobs noted.
"Both Congress and the general American workplace were designed by and for men who had often stay-at-home spouses who handled all of the domestic work," she said.
"It's going to take a lot of work for us to create a society where the domestic work is really shared equally between women and men."
In the meantime, Jacobs feels reassured to have a back-up plan for whenever she does feel she can fit children into her busy career.
"I hope to be able to do that one day, but I just haven't figured the time is right just yet."

title: FPCCI demands rollback of high taxes on hybrid cars
description: Calls for notifying new auto policy immediately.
author: Mohammad Hussain Khan
content:
HYDERABAD: The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI) has expressed concern over the sales tax hike on hybrid vehicles, from 8.5 per cent to 25pc, and warned that this short-sighted policy would hurt consumers and cripple the auto industry.
In a statement issued on Saturday, Adeel Siddiqui, a member of the FPCCI Executive Committee, noted that tax concessions on hybrid vehicles expired on June 30 and with no new auto policy notified in time, the Federal Board of Revenue restored the general sales tax rate of 25pc on hybrid electric vehicles and plug-in hybrid vehicles.
He said that this represented a massive increase from earlier preferential rates of 8.5pc for hybrids up to 1800cc and 12.75pc for those above 1800cc.
So, he said, the auto industry was in chaos and automakers have temporarily halted production and stopped issuing invoices because they do not know which sales tax rate to apply.
Calls for notifying new auto policy immediately
He said that a production halt affected thousands of workers, vendors, and transporters, as well as factory workers, who were losing work and wages due to this policy vacuum.
He stated that Pakistan’s energy security was at risk, as it imports about 80pc of its petroleum products, making transport electrification a matter of national security.
He said that the government was discouraging fuel-efficient vehicles and keeping the country dependent on expensive imported fuel by making hybrids more expensive.
Secondly, he said, investor confidence was eroding, and policy uncertainty was damaging it in new-energy vehicle projects.
He said that policy remained regressive, wondering why the government was increasing taxes on hybrids — which offer lower running costs and reduced fuel consumption — while reportedly considering tax relief on vehicles priced above Rs10m. He said that this sends a confusing signal about the government’s policy priorities.
He called for an immediate rollback of 25pc sales tax on hybrid vehicles, or at least a reduction to 18pc until the new auto policy was finalised.
He demanded that Auto Policy 2026-31 should be notified without delay to provide clarity and stability to the industry. He stressed the need for a phased transition to clean energy with incentives tied to local manufacturing and technology transfer.
He said that current policy was a self-inflicted wound that would slow Pakistan’s transition to fuel-efficient vehicles, increase fuel import costs, and damage the auto industry at a time when it was showing signs of recovery.
He said that it was high time to act before damage was done to Pakistan’s automotive sector and energy security.

title: Medal ceremonies delayed at European Athletics Championships in Birmingham due to arrest
description: Transport was also delayed because of the arrest, leading to crowds building up outside the venue.
author: Shannen Headley
content:
Thousands of members of the crowd were unable to leave the event as transport was suspended
Medal ceremonies at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham were postponed after a man was arrested on suspicion of fraud.
West Midlands Police said concerns were raised after a man was found in an area of Alexander Stadium on Saturday evening without the right accreditation.
Transport at the tournament was suspended as a result of the arrest and necessary security procedures.
Members of the crowd reported being held outside by security staff for more than an hour after the event finished, with a large police presence at the scene.
The evening session concluded with Great Britain winning a pair of gold medals in the men's and women's 4x100m relays.
Tournament organisers said transport was suspended while the necessary security measures took place, but operations had returned to normal in the early hours of Sunday.
A statement from Birmingham 2026 said: "The safety and wellbeing of our spectators, athletes, workforce and the wider Championships' family will always be our first priority.
"We recognise that the delays presented challenges for those affected and would like to thank everyone for their patience, understanding and cooperation throughout the evening."
More information relating to the postponed medal ceremonies is due to be released later.
A West Midlands Police spokesperson said a man in his 30s remained in custody for questioning.
The crowd at the Alexander Stadium appeared to be near its 23,000 capacity.
At one point during the session, there was an announcement that the six medal ceremonies, scheduled to take place after the final event between 22:00 and 23:00 BST were cancelled, understood to be in relation to the police incident.
People posted on social media, reporting "crazy queues" for the shuttle bus and blue flashing lights on the main road outside the stadium.
A statement on the event's official account, posted on X at 23:03, said: "We apologise for the significant delays in leaving the Alexander Stadium venue this evening.
"Buses and coaches will start to arrive and departures will begin to gradually take place.
"We thank you for your patience with this matter. Please listen to the instructions from the safety personnel and marshals who are there to support you."

content:
President and Prime Minister pay tribute to Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, leaders and workers of Pakistan Movement
Updated Friday Aug 14 2026
Millions of Pakistanis are celebrating 79 years of Independence Day on Friday, filling the country with vibrant patriotic fervour, flag-hoisting ceremonies, and solemn prayers for the future.
The dawn in Pakistan was ushered in by the boom of a 31-gun salute in the federal capital and a 21-gun salute in the provincial headquarters. Special prayers were offered at mosques across the country for peace, solidarity and prosperity of the country.
The major cities across the country have been transformed into a green and white theme, with the streets and buildings adorned with bunting lights and flags. Special Independence Day ceremonies are also being held in schools, colleges and public institutions.
People from all sectors have expressed their commitment to national unity, peace and development of the country, with President Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paying tribute to Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the leaders and workers of the Pakistan Movement and all those who gave up their homes, security and livelihoods in the struggle for a homeland.
