title: Avalanche risk, bad weather disrupt climbing season in Gilgit-Baltistan
description: No climber managed to summit K2, Gasherbrum-I this summer.
author: Jamil Nagri
content:
GILGIT: Climate change-induced shifts in weather patterns have worsened conditions on the peaks of the Karakoram Range in Gilgit-Baltistan, creating serious difficulties for mountaineers.
No climber managed to summit the world’s second-highest mountain, K2 (8,611 metres), or Gasherbrum-I (8,080 metres), this summer.
Around 40 foreign climbers also failed to reach the summits of Gasherbrum-II (8,035 metres), Broad Peak (8,047 metres) and Nanga Parbat (8,126 metres) this year.
Persistent storms, heavy snowfall, unstable snow conditions and an exceptionally high avalanche risk created hurdles for climbers attempting to summit peaks in Gilgit-Baltistan, particularly five of the 14 eight-thousanders.
No climber managed to summit K2, Gasherbrum-I this summer
Expedition teams usually spend weeks at base camps assessing weather forecasts, fixing ropes and acclimatising before beginning their summit push.
Mountaineers have experienced persistent bad weather, avalanches, rockfalls, strong winds and unpredictable conditions at the peaks during the summer season for the past two years. The climbing season on the Karakoram peaks, including K2, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum-I and Gasherbrum-II, usually runs from the end of July to mid-August.
Ghulam Muhammad, a tour operator, told Dawn that more than 200 climbers attempted to summit K2, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum-II and Gasherbrum-I this year. “This year, continued bad weather kept teams at base camp, while repeated summit attempts were called off due to unsafe conditions on the mountains.”
He said only three foreign expedition groups reached the summit of Gasherbrum-II, while members of one local expedition team successfully summited Broad Peak. Earlier, two expedition teams had summited Nanga Parbat, where the climbing season closes by the end of June.
Ayaz Shigri, general secretary of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, told Dawn that weather conditions at the peaks remained unstable this summer. However, he said that after the devastating tragedy at Broad Peak on July 30, in which 10 foreign climbers, including Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, lost their lives when a snow avalanche struck them during their summit attempt, many climbers at K2 and Gasherbrum-I abandoned their missions and joined the search and rescue operation.
Asghar Porik, another tour operator, said shifting weather patterns in the mountains had made it difficult for mountaineers to plan their summit attempts. “For 100 or 500 years, climbers have planned their attempts in the Karakoram according to established weather patterns. They usually attempt K2 between July 20 and August 15, with the weather generally considered suitable until the end of June,” he said.
He said the situation had worsened in recent years as rising temperatures made snow unstable and increased the risks of avalanches and rockfalls. Asghar Porik added that his 11-member expedition team at Gasherbrum-II could not find a suitable weather window and called off its expedition.
Ikram Baig, president of the GB Association of Tour Operators, said Broad Peak was considered one of the comparatively less dangerous eight-thousanders. “Broad Peak is often described by experienced mountaineers as one of the comparatively less technical 8,000-metre peaks. However, fresh snowfall can make even an easier route extremely dangerous by creating unstable snow conditions and a high risk of avalanches,” he said.
Mr Baig said climate change had altered conditions and made the environment at the peaks increasingly uncertain. Mohammad Ali Nagari, a tour operator, said the growing number of commercial expeditions was also degrading the fragile environment at the peaks.
Ayaz Shigri said the summer climbing season on the Karakoram peaks had now closed, with climbers returning from the eight-thousanders without summiting K2 or Gasherbrum-I this year. Last year, too, foreign climbers faced similar conditions and mostly returned without summiting peaks in GB.

title: ‘No no-go areas’ across Balochistan, says Home Minister Langove
description: Minister says terrorists use violence as a cover for extortion, intimidation at the directive of external forces.
author: Saleem Shahid
content:
QUETTA: Balochistan Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langove has said there were no “no-go areas” in the province, though terrorists remained active along the Quetta-Karachi national highway and security forces were conducting operations against them.
Speaking at a press conference here on Saturday, Mr Langove accused armed groups of carrying out terrorism and extortion in the name of an “independence struggle” and urged people to support the state and national institutions in the fight against terrorism.
Mr Langove thanked the people of Balochistan for celebrating Independence Day with enthusiasm and praised the security forces for maintaining security across the province.
He highlighted healthcare facilities provided in Kalat and Khaliqabad, saying residents, particularly women, had previously faced difficulties transporting patients to hospitals because ambulances were unavailable. The government had provided 30 to 35 ambulances in the two areas, he said, but alleged that terrorists had taken them away.
Minister says terrorists use violence as a cover for extortion, intimidation at the directive of external forces
According to Mr Langove, women had appealed to the terrorists in the name of the Quran not to take the ambulances, but their pleas were ignored. He said the groups were not fighting for independence or people’s rights but were depriving local communities of basic facilities and trying to impose their narrative on young people and women.
The minister said that terrorist groups were backed by India and Afghanistan and that their leaders were controlled by external forces. He also accused terrorists of collecting extortion money from local landowners.
He urged the Baloch people to consider the future of their children and stay away from violence while cooperating with the government and state institutions.
Responding to a question, Mr Langove acknowledged the presence of terrorists along the Quetta-Karachi RCD National Highway. He said government action against terrorists was sometimes criticised by political and public circles and urged them to support the state in dealing with the security situation.
The minister also disclosed that his convoy came under attack while he was returning from Kalat after attending Independence Day events. He said he was travelling in an SSP vehicle when terrorists attempted to target his vehicle.
One of the vehicles in the convoy came under fire during an exchange of gunfire. Police, the Anti-Terrorism Force and Frontier Corps personnel accompanying him confronted the attackers.
Six security personnel were injured, he said. They were evacuated and taken to Shaheed Nawab Ghous Bakhsh Raisani Hospital before being shifted to the Trauma Centre in Quetta after receiving initial treatment.

title: World leaders, friendly nations wish Pakistan peace, prosperity on Independence Day
description: Iranian president stresses greater bilateral coordination.Marco Rubio reaffirms enduring US-Pakistan partnership.Pakistan, Russia cooperating on regional issues: Putin.World leaders and friendly nations extended Independence Day...
author: Web Desk
content:
Published August 14, 2026
World leaders and friendly nations extended Independence Day greetings to Pakistan on Friday, as the country marked 79 years of independence with special prayers and events honouring the sacrifices of its founding fathers.
The day began with a 31-gun salute in Islamabad and a 21-gun salute in the provincial capitals. An elegant change of guard ceremony was also held at the Mazar-e-Quaid mausoleum in Karachi.
In his message, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian termed Pakistan's Independence Day a "valuable opportunity to pay tribute to the achievements of the great Pakistani nation".
The Iranian president said that Tehran and Islamabad's shared interests and destinies were more closely linked than ever, stressing that the need for greater coordination and cooperation between the two countries had also increased.
President Pezeshkian reaffirmed Iran's commitment to further strengthening comprehensive ties with Pakistan.
He also said Iran was ready to take more effective steps to strengthen bilateral relations by drawing on mutual trust, respect and the two states' existing wide-ranging potential.
The Iranian president also prayed for Pakistan's development, prosperity and elevation, and the consolidation of the longstanding brotherly relations between the two nations.
Separately, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman congratulated President Asif Ali Zardari on Pakistan’s Independence Day.
According to Saudi media, the Saudi leadership expressed its best wishes for Pakistan’s development, prosperity and stability, while reaffirming its resolve to further strengthen the longstanding ties between the two brotherly countries.
Similarly, Chinese embassy in Pakistan in its post on X expressed "heartfelt congratulations to our brothers and sisters in Pakistan" on celebrating their Independence Day.
"Wishing Pakistan eternal peace and prosperity. Hand in hand, our ironclad friendship will continue to thrive. Chin–Pak Dosti Zindabad," it posted.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio extended "heartfelt congratulations" to the people of Pakistan on the country's Independence Day.
"Through our mutual cooperation in areas such as regional mediation, critical minerals, energy, counterterrorism, cultural heritage, and trade and investment, we are transforming our shared capabilities into progress and delivering real results for both the American and Pakistani peoples," he said in a statement posted to the official X account of the US embassy in Islamabad.
Rubio reaffirmed the enduring partnership between the two nations and the longstanding friendship between their two peoples.
Russian President Vladimir Putin extended Independence Day greetings to President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, wishing for peace, prosperity and well-being for the people of Pakistan.
"Russia-Pakistan relations are developing successfully," Putin said in his message.
The Russian president said that the two countries were continuing fruitful cooperation in political, trade, economic, humanitarian and other fields.
He added that the Kremlin and Islamabad were also maintaining cooperation on important regional and global issues.
Putin expressed confidence that the two countries would further strengthen all areas of their bilateral partnership in the mutual interests of their peoples.
Meanwhile, Bahrain Crown Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa also extended greetings to Pakistan on its Independence Day.
Turkiye, which recently signed a joint defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, congratulated the "friendly and brotherly Pakistan" on Independence Day.
Similarly, Azerbaijan extended heartfelt congratulations to Pakistan on 79 years of independence.
Congratulating Pakistan on Independence Day, Egypt's foreign ministry said that Cairo looked forward to further deepening historic friendship and strengthening partnership for the benefit of two peoples.
Germany's Ambassador to Pakistan, Ina Lepel, shared a video message on social media, congratulating Pakistanis on 79 years of independence.
In a video posted on the German embassy in Islamabad's official Facebook account, Ambassador Lepel expressed hope for peace, prosperity, and development in the country and stronger Pakistan-Germany ties.
Separately, former Maldives President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih extended greetings and best wishes to President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and the people of Pakistan on the country.
In a message shared on social media, Solih expressed hope that the longstanding fraternal ties between the Maldives and Pakistan would grow even stronger.
“On the occasion of Pakistan’s 79th anniversary of independence, I extend my greetings and best wishes to President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and the people of Pakistan,” he said.
“May the fraternal ties that have long existed between Maldives and Pakistan grow even stronger,” Solih added.

title: Pakistan, Norway agree to expand cooperation on counterterrorism, illegal immigration
description: Naqvi says effective measures cut illegal immigration by 47%.FM Eide praises Pakistan's role in easing US-Iran tensions.Interior minister raises terrorism concerns linked to Afghanistan.Pakistan and Norway have agreed to enhance...
author: Web Desk
content:
Published August 14, 2026
Pakistan and Norway have agreed to enhance cooperation in combating terrorism, illegal immigration, police training and mutual legal assistance as the two countries sought to further strengthen bilateral collaboration on security and law enforcement matters.
The understanding was reached during a meeting between Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide on Friday, the Ministry of Interior said in a statement.
The two sides held detailed discussions on bilateral relations, regional developments and issues of mutual interest.
Naqvi said Pakistan's effective measures had resulted in a 47% reduction in illegal immigration and reiterated that the country had adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards the practice.
He added that Pakistan's efforts had been acknowledged by the European Union (EU) and stressed that promoting legal migration was essential for effectively tackling irregular migration.
The meeting also discussed the activities of banned organisations operating from Afghanistan.
The interior minister said Afghan territory continued to be used for terrorism against Pakistan, adding that the country stood as a barrier between the world and terrorism.
He emphasised the need for collective efforts to completely eliminate the threat.
FM Eide praised Pakistan's role in helping reduce tensions between the United States and Iran and discussed the broader regional situation.
He also commended the contribution of the Pakistani community in Norway, noting that it played an important role in various sectors of Norwegian society.
Naqvi said the Norwegian foreign minister's visit would prove to be an important milestone in further strengthening relations between the two countries.
FM Eide arrived in Pakistan on Thursday at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.
A day ago, DPM Dar and his Norwegian counterpart held a restricted-format meeting before leading delegation-level talks at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The two sides reviewed the full spectrum of bilateral relations and held in-depth discussions on regional and international developments of mutual interest, the Foreign Office said in a statement.
Addressing a joint press conference after the talks, DPM Dar said Pakistan attaches great importance to its relations with Norway and is committed to further deepening bilateral cooperation.
FM Eide lauded Pakistan's efforts to advance regional and international peace, noting that these initiatives had garnered international recognition.
Norwegian FM Eide-led high-level delegation also called on Field Marshal Asim Munir at the General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi, where the two sides discussed regional security, bilateral relations and matters of mutual interest.

title: Formula E: Taylor Barnard on the end-of-season races in London
description: Taylor Barnard, 22, says talented young drivers often get shut out because of financial issues.
author: Naomi Clarke
content:
Taylor Barnard is the youngest driver to secure a podium, pole and points in Formula E
Making split-second decisions while driving up to 200mph probably seems like a crazy task for most of us.
But Britain's youngest Formula E driver is learning to take it in his stride as his second season in the series draws to a close.
Back in 2024, Taylor Barnard became the youngest person to start an E-Prix and since then he's broken several other records - including becoming the youngest driver to secure a podium, pole and points in the sport.
So what's the 22-year-old got his sights set on now? The ultimate title, of course, world champion.
Barnard tells BBC Newsbeat he feels he got into racing by the "skin of my teeth", due to the extreme costs it takes to climb the motorsport ladder.
The immense financial backing needed to become a professional driver has been long known, with stars like Sir Lewis Hamilton speaking openly about the sacrifices his family made to get him a seat in Formula 1.
And Barnard feels if he was trying to climb the ranks now, he wouldn't make it due to prices being "so blown out of proportion".
Barnard says fans can expect to see a lot of the cars going "side-by-side [at] almost every corner"
Barnard, who's from Norwich, says the driving bug was passed down from his father, who was a karting driver in his younger years.
He rose through the ranks of British and European karting, before his talent helped him secure backing to get through Formula 3 and 2.
Barnard finally secured a seat in Formula E with McLaren, and transferred to DS Penske for the current season.
"It sounds very simple but trust me, it's anything but that," he says.
"It's super expensive, super difficult. And where my family and I've come from, we've always been on the difficult end of that journey."
The driver recalls being raised in a "very normal, working family", and at one stage they had to re-mortgage their house so Barnard could continue his racing career.
"We really did put everything on the line for me to be able to make it," he says.
"I would be lying if we're still not stinging from when we did that."
Now that he's getting paid as a professional, he says he's trying to pay his parents back "for everything they've done".
Barnard also wants to support young talented drivers who he feels are being left behind - as he feels not everybody that's made it into top-flight sports "deserves to be there".
"There's definitely people that have bought their way in or haven't earned their way," he says.
"And there's definitely been people out there, younger guys or girls that have the talent and the skill to be able to make it, which just gets shut out by financial issues.
"That's not right. And the way that it's going in the last few years, it's only getting worse."
Barnard says he's not sure how motorsport's governing body the FIA or racing teams can best address this issue as he recognises it is a business.
There are various academies and driver development programmes run by professional teams, but they are often very competitive.
An FIA spokesperson told Newsbeat "improving accessibility and affordability in motorsport is a core priority" for the governing body.
They added that some costs connected with competing, such as travel and team operations, were "outside the FIA's direct remit" but it was "committed to taking decisive action and investing in global initiatives".
Among the programmes, it said, its affordable cross car, girls on track and global karting plan look to lower "financial barriers" and expand "access to talented drivers around the world".
Barnard made his Formula E debut with McLaren, but raced for DS Penske this season
Barnard's journey has made him "appreciate the little things a lot more", he says.
And the end of this season will be made sweeter as he gets to drive in front of his family and friends at his home race when the 2025-2026 series closes at London's Excel this weekend.
It will be a tense double-header as nine drivers were in contention for the championship title going into the last two races.
Barnard's future for next season is still slightly uncertain as DS Automobiles, the manufacturer behind his team, is set to leave the sport.
And with Penske yet to confirm its plans for the next era of Formula E cars, dubbed Gen4, the young Brit is focused on finishing the season on a high.
Barnard says fans can expect to see a lot of the grid going "side-by-side [at] almost every corner" and probably "a few crashes".
"Throughout the weekend we obviously do the duals in qualifying, which is super exciting.
"Next year the cars are going to be even faster, which is going to be even more exciting.
"I would actually argue Formula E has the best racing that you can view anywhere."

title: South Korean president proposes talks with North to formally end war
description: Two countries are still at war since their 1950s confrontation ended without a peace treaty.
author: AFP
content:
SEOUL: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung proposed talks with North Korea on Saturday to formally end the long-running Korean war, as Pyongyang deepens ties with Moscow while asserting its status as an “irreversible” nuclear state.
The two Koreas remain technically at war because their 1950-53 conflict ended with an armistice rather than a peace treaty.
Lee made the proposal in his speech at a ceremony marking the anniversary of Korea’s liberation from Japan’s 1910-45 colonial rule.
“Let us put down our intention to threaten each other and begin discussions to end the long-running war as the directly involved parties,” Lee said in his speech.
Two countries are still at war since their 1950s confrontation ended without a peace treaty
“Through this, it may also be possible to discuss effective measures to halt the advancement of North Korea’s nuclear capabilities,” he added.
Lee’s proposal came as North Korea this week denounced upcoming annual US-South Korean military drills, warning of stronger deterrence measures.
Pyongyang has also recently been bristling over Tokyo’s gradual military build-up in the Pacific, firing off two missiles in as many weeks after the latter pledged to up its defence capabilities with a “sense of urgency and crisis”.
North Korea has repeatedly declared itself an “irreversible” nuclear state since a 2019 summit between Kim and US counterpart Donald Trump in Hanoi collapsed over the scope of denuclearisation and sanctions relief.
South Korea’s dovish President Lee has reversed the stance of his hawkish predecessor since taking power in June last year, offering the nuclear-armed North talks without preconditions.
Last month, South Korea’s unification minister even claimed Seoul had abandoned its campaign prioritising pressure on the North to dismantle its nuclear weapons, focusing instead on halting the expansion of Pyongyang’s nuclear activities.
The hermetic leadership of North Korea has yet to respond to Lee’s repeated offers, and has instead bolstered military ties with Russia.
Analysts say Pyongyang is receiving financial support, food, energy and military technology from Moscow for supplying troops and munitions for Russia’s war in Ukraine.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is expected to visit Russia later this year, potentially to discuss further weapons supplies to Moscow.
Washington, Seoul’s key security ally, stations about 28,500 troops in South Korea to bolster the country’s defences against military threats from Pyongyang.
Colonel Ryan Donald, spokesman for the US and South Korean combined forces command, said this week that North Korea’s deployment to the European war had changed the threat his soldiers may face on the Korean peninsula.
“They’ve taken those lessons they learned there and brought them back to North Korea,” he told reporters as he talked about the 11-day South Korea-US joint exercises due to begin on Monday.
“Our training accounts for that threat.”

title: Political rivals should not let differences turn into animosity, says Nawaz
description: Congratulates winners of elections in AJK, calls PPP's comments "upsetting".
author: News Desk
content:
PML-N supremo and former prime minister Nawaz Sharif said on Saturday that while political differences between opponents were common during elections, they should never turn into animosity, apparently referring to the deepening differences between the ruling party and its coalition partner, the PPP, at the Centre.
Elections are being held across AJK in three phases amid tensions between protesters and the authorities that have been ongoing for over two months.
Addressing a party convention in Murree, the party president congratulated the winners of the elections in AJK, while extending commiserations to the losing candidates. However, he noted that the complaints from the PPP have been “upsetting”.
“We have always maintained good relations with our opponents. There is always disagreement in politics, but it should not reach the point where it creates animosity,” he said. “This is unacceptable.”
The PML-N supremo noted that AJK’s atmosphere has always been good, but lamented seeing the buildup of enmity.
“I was upset over their losses, and I have good relations with them personally,” Nawaz said. “We need to look at those factors that contributed to their defeat. We had very good candidates who bravely contested these elections. If they were defeated, we must look at the reasons why.”
He noted, “We can lose seats, but we cannot lose our spirit”.
“God has granted us victory in these conditions. As you know, there have been three phases in these elections; the third phase has yet to conclude. But God granted us a majority in the first two phases. We cannot thank Him enough,” Nawaz added, warning that there is “no room” for hurting public sentiment.
The PML-N supremo opined that this is the first time that such an environment was created in AJK. He attributed it to successive governments failing to fulfil their duties and meet the needs and requests of the people, regardless of which ever party was in power.
“We absolutely need to enable progress in AJK, whatever way we can. We need to resolve problems there, and we will do what we’ve done in Punjab there,” Nawaz stressed.
“It should be our duty, and we need to fulfil public sentiment. If, God forbid, we fail to deliver, the people of AJK will grow angry, and the reason behind it is valid. We would then need to look inward.”
The PML-N supremo noted that the region needs a great deal of development and tasked Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to provide AJK with as much funding as possible to build roads, hospitals, and ensure people have livelihoods.
“Tourism needs to be promoted, and industry must be established. Agriculture requires our full attention, and [we can provide] agricultural loans like those in Punjab,” he added.
Moreover, he said that people in Punjab are receiving loans for their houses and expressed his intention to launch such schemes in AJK.
“I will absolutely direct Shehbaz sahib to launch these schemes in this region, and besides that, provide funding,” Nawaz declared.
“People [need to] feel that they are being granted their rights. The people of AJK look at Punjab’s roads, hospitals and hope they are built in AJK; AJK’s children want laptops in their hands, and people should receive Kisaan cards and livelihoods.”
Nawaz further said that the rest of Pakistan was moving forward and was different from the past, while hailing Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s efforts and vowing that the current problems would be resolved very soon.
“Punjab is changing, and AJK should be changed in the same way,” he emphasised.
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif spoke about the PPP’s allegations of electoral rigging in the AJK polls, saying that it should “consider the logic” of making such claims.
“It is upsetting that they (PPP) made false allegations of rigging against the PML-N. When they won in Gilgit-Baltistan, they made no claims of rigging; where they lost, they made these allegations,” she told the party conference.
She added that the PPP could not promise the people of AJK new roads and a clean atmosphere, as they were unable to provide those to the people of Sindh.
“In making these allegations, they forgot that the government, administration, president, prime minister and staff were theirs. They should consider logic when levelling allegations against others,” she added.
The polls are being held in phases amid unrest in the region.
The PML-N bagged 24 seats — nine from Mirpur division in the first phase on July 27 and 15 in the second phase on Aug 2 , comprising Muzaffarabad Division and the 12 refugee seats. The PPP, on the other hand, won only 10 constituencies during these phases.
The third phase, held on Monday, was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district.
However, the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation.
Elections in 23 polling stations of the two constituencies, which had been postponed earlier, were held today.
The PPP has criticised the conduct of the AJK elections, with a high-level meeting of the party in Islamabad terming the polls “rigged and violent” and expressing serious concern over the role of the AJK Election Commission.
Earlier this week, a meeting chaired by PPP Women’s Wing president and AJK affairs in-charge Faryal Talpur, also criticised the phase-wise conduct of the elections and demanded the immediate completion of polling in the remaining two districts of the third phase and seven constituencies of Poonch so that the Legislative Assembly could be fully constituted.
The participants raised questions over the suspension of internet services, shortages of polling material and staff at some polling stations, and alleged inadequate security arrangements.

title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: POLITICS OF THE BIG TENT
description: The very diversity that makes big-tent parties electorally powerful can also become their greatest vulnerability.
author: Nadeem F. Paracha
content:
In Europe and the United States, the post-1945 era marked a shift from ‘mass parties’ to broad ‘big-tent’ parties. Mass parties had operated on strict class lines. Democratic socialist outfits appealed to industrial workers, while conservative parties represented business elites and religious traditionalists.
Big-tent politics had already taken root in North America due to its vast geography, rapid industrialisation, and diverse immigrant and Black populations. To build winning national majorities, the Democratic and Republican parties developed broad platforms, accommodating competing internal factions under a shared umbrella and a loose ideological core. This was the beginning of big-tent parties.
The Democratic Party in the US, especially from the early 1930s onwards, has housed democratic socialists, progressives, social liberals and pro-business centrists, alongside its conservative Southern wing, which existed within the party till the early 1960s. The latter was mainly to bag votes from the ‘Bible belt’ states. The modern Republican Party functions as a broad umbrella encompassing social conservatives, Christian nationalists, fiscal centrists and right-wing populists.
A similar evolution occurred in western Europe after World War II. According to the German jurist Otto Kirchheimer, as the post-war economic growth expanded the middle-class, most voters began to favour pragmatic moderation over class antagonism. Left-wing parties, such as the UK Labour Party and Germany’s Social Democratic Party, shifted toward a progressive centre-left stance, while centre-right parties, such as the British Conservatives and Germany’s Christian Democrats, softened their hard social moralism and elitism to capture votes from across the classes.
Political scientists mostly view big-tent parties as important democratic stabilisers. By absorbing diverse economic, regional and social groups, a big-tent outfit facilitates them to negotiate and form a consensus under a single umbrella. This prevents extreme polarisation and avoids the chaotic parliamentary fragmentation typical of unstable multiparty systems that lack big-tent parties.
From the Democrats and Republicans in the United States to the PPP, PML-N and PTI in Pakistan, the very diversity that makes big-tent parties electorally powerful can also become their greatest vulnerability
Big-tent outfits combine diverse demands and elements, transforming societal rivalries into organised, workable governing units. The success of a big-tent party depends on how they design mechanisms to manage internal dissent. Rather than enforcing monolithic obedience, party structures use primary elections, regional quotas and factional appointments to give diverse interest groups a seat at tables that matter.
This internal diplomacy allows the overarching party to remain flexible. A well-managed big-tent party can position its platform across different political cycles, moving slightly leftward or rightward to keep pace with  changing electorate moods, without suffering an electoral decline.
Following the 1947 Partition , India saw a classic big-tent system emerge under the Indian National Congress (INC). Operating on a secular, centre-left platform, Congress absorbed diverse socialist, moderate and regional groups to maintain a 30-year political monopoly. As the nation’s founding party, it offered a shared national brand that co-opted multiple local political elites and bridged vast linguistic and religious divides.
INC’s dominance was broken in 1977 by the Janata Party (JP). JP was a broad anti-INC coalition of secular, regional, Hindutva and left-wing groups who couldn’t find a place under INC’s tent. However, JP illustrated a common pitfall related to big-tent politics: unmanaged factional infighting. Driven by intense ideological friction and personal rivalries among its leadership, JP collapsed from within after just three years in power.
When internal fractures widen in big-tent parties, the parties tend to lose their electoral appeal or fall prey to radical internal takeovers. This occurred within the US Republican Party, where the right-wing populist Maga (Make America Great Again) movement led by Donald Trump weaponised primary elections to displace the Republican Party’s dominant free market and moderate factions.
The populist wing of the party then reoriented the outfit into becoming a nationalist-populist vehicle. But this transformation has introduced severe vulnerabilities, driven by infighting within the party’s populist wing, foreign policy controversies and an increasing backlash in the US against Israeli lobby groups such as the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac). Trump’s approval ratings have plummeted .
The Democrats are facing their own internal tensions. Key primary victories by progressive candidates of the party have alarmed its centrist factions, who fear left-leaning Democrats could alienate moderate voters in upcoming national contests.
In South Asia, apart from INC and then JP, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) began to function as a big-tent party. Historically a Hindu nationalist party with an upper-caste base, the BJP began to widen its umbrella. It started to accommodate distinct groups: Hindutva hardliners, big business groups, populists and pragmatists absorbed from opposition parties. Hindutva remains the BJP’s ideological anchor, though, even as it increasingly applies big-tent electoral strategies.
Pakistan developed a big-tent model led by the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N). Before these, Pakistan’s founding party, the Muslim League, had successfully managed to combine a wide range of left to right groups to win enough seats in the 1946 elections in British India, which allowed it to push for a separate Muslim-majority country. But after the creation of Pakistan, friction between different groups in the League became so intense that the party fractured.
The PPP, formed in 1967, shaped a centre-left core with diverse leftist, progressive, liberal and centrist groups, while the PML-N, formed in 1992, united urban pro-business cohorts, landed elites, centrists and social conservatives. In 2011, facilitated by the then military establishment, the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) expanded into a third big-tent party by absorbing traditional ‘electables’ from the two existing big-tent outfits.
PTI operated as an archetypal contemporary populist party, weaving a flexible and performative core of right- and left-wing tropes around a central anti-corruption narrative and personal loyalty to its leader. This vague ideological architecture allowed urban middle-class youth, conservatives, landed elites and mainstream Islamists to coexist under one banner. However, like India’s Janata Party, PTI struggled to manage its internal frictions and rapidly unravelled once its top leader was removed from power and imprisoned.
Big-tent parties remain double-edged constructs. While their capacity to combine diverse interests and build broad platforms shields democracies against fragmentation, their reliance on a conflicted ideological core and mismanaged internal conflicts leaves them vulnerable. This requires continuous maintenance. Without disciplined leadership, big-tent parties risk devolving into factional warfare, opening the door to radical takeovers or collapse when internal consensus breaks down. Maintaining a workable equilibrium remains a constant challenge.
In Pakistan, big-tent parties such as the PML-N and the PPP have done remarkably well to avoid disintegration despite attempts by previous military establishments to dismantle them by exploiting their internal frictions. This ability to regroup and survive is something that PTI has, so far, failed to demonstrate.

title: Celebratory gunfire injures nearly 100 across Karachi, claims one life
description: Injured included 17 children, 10 women: rescue officials.Police arrest 30 suspects, recover multiple weapons.Security guard among suspects held over aerial firing.Independence Day celebrations turned deadly across Karachi as...
author: Web Desk
content:
Published August 14, 2026
Independence Day celebrations turned deadly across Karachi as celebratory aerial firing left one woman dead and 94 others injured, including 17 children, rescue officials said on Friday.
An Edhi Foundation spokesperson confirmed the injury toll had climbed to 94, with the wounded comprising 10 women, 17 children and 59 men. The woman's death, rescue sources said, occurred during the same wave of celebratory gunfire that swept the city.
The injured were taken to Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, Civil Hospital and Abbasi Shaheed Hospital for treatment, rescue officials said.
Hospital officials gave a breakdown of the casualties brought in over the course of the night. Abbasi Shaheed Hospital received 24 patients, including one woman, four children and 19 men, while Jinnah Hospital took in 35 people, among them three children, four women and 28 men.
Civil Hospital's trauma centre, meanwhile, treated 26 patients, including 10 children, four women and 12 men, hospital administration said.
The firing incidents were reported from several parts of the city, including Lyari, Saddar, Korangi, Malir, Azizabad, North Nazimabad, Nazimabad, Gulbahar, Gulshan-e-Iqbal, Orangi Town, Jamshed Quarters and Defence.
Police said they had arrested 30 suspects allegedly involved in aerial firing from Karachi's eastern, western and central districts.
The arrests were made in areas including Hyderi Market, Bilal Colony, Liaquatabad, New Karachi, Taimuria, Azizabad, Joharabad and Gulbahar, police said, adding that arrests were also made within the jurisdictions of Khwaja Ajmer Nagri, Samanabad, Rizvia Society and Sir Syed police stations.
Police said various types of weapons were recovered from the suspects.
In Gulshan-e-Iqbal, police arrested a security guard allegedly involved in aerial firing and recovered a weapon from him, police said. Two other suspects were arrested from Orangi Town and Iqbal Market over alleged involvement in aerial firing, according to the SSP West.
In an unrelated incident at a hotel in Paposh Nagar's Sarafa Bazaar, a woman was killed when a pistol allegedly discharged accidentally, police said.
According to police, the pistol was placed on a table with a round still in its chamber. It discharged when the weapon was being handled, striking the woman.
She was taken to Abbasi Shaheed Hospital, where she later died.
Police arrested the accused, identified as Imran, and recovered a 9mm pistol from him. The suspect is the woman's cousin, according to police.
Authorities have repeatedly warned residents against aerial firing during celebrations, saying bullets fired into the air can fall back to the ground and seriously injure or kill people.
Karachi has witnessed repeated casualties from celebratory firing during Independence Day festivities in recent years. In 2025, three people were killed and at least 75 others were injured in similar incidents. In 2024, about 95 people were injured in aerial firing incidents during Independence Day celebrations.

title: Nation celebrates Pakistan's Independence Day with zeal, national spirit
description: President Zardari pays tribute to martyrs of armed forces.Pakistan's security linked to global peace, stability: president.Pakistan moving towards goal of a developed economy: PM.The top political leadership of Pakistan stressed...
author: Web Desk
content:
Published August 14, 2026
The top political leadership of Pakistan stressed the need for stability, reforms and global peace as the nation marks 79 years of independence on Friday.
The nation is celebrating Independence Day with zeal and fervour, with special prayers offered at mosques across the country for peace, solidarity and prosperity of the country.
The day began with a 31-gun salute in the federal capital and a 21-gun salute in the provincial capitals. An elegant change of guard ceremony was also held at the Mazar-e-Quaid mausoleum in Karachi.
On the occasion, President Zardari paid tribute to Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the leaders and workers of the Pakistan Movement and all those who gave up their homes, security and livelihoods in the struggle for a homeland.
In his message, the president said that independence was not only a historic achievement, but a responsibility that each generation must carry forward.
"The Pakistan that was created through the democratic will of its people must continue to grow stronger, more secure and more prosperous. Our task is not only to remember what earlier generations achieved, but to add to it through our own work," he added.
Reflecting on the past year, he said that Marka-e-Haq demonstrated that Pakistan sought peace, but also possesses the resolve and capacity to defend its sovereignty and national interests.
A country that can defend itself must also use its strength to prevent conflict, protect peace and serve the interests of its people, he added.
President Zardari also paid tribute to the martyrs of the armed forces, law enforcement agencies and police. "Their courage and commitment have helped safeguard our nation against external aggression and the threat of terrorism. The people of Pakistan remain deeply grateful for their service."
On the country's global diplomacy, he said that Islamabad has effectively used its channels of communication, its geographical location and diplomatic capital to encourage dialogue and de-escalation at a time when wider conflict in the Middle East could have serious consequences for the region and the world.
"Pakistan's approach is clear. We believe that disputes, no matter how serious, must ultimately be addressed through dialogue and diplomacy," he added.
Pakistan's security is linked to the peace and stability of its neighbourhood and the world, he said, emphasising that the country will continue to support efforts that reduce tensions, protect regional stability and create conditions for cooperation.
On the domestic front, the president called for strengthening the economy, creating greater opportunities for youth and bolstering institutions through a series of governance, economic and social reforms.
Terming youth Pakistan's greatest strength, he said that it was the government's responsibility to give young people the education, skills and opportunities they need to realise their potential.
President Zardari also renewed solidarity with the people of Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir, reaffirming support for their legitimate struggle for their rights.
"Pakistan will continue to support a peaceful resolution of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with the aspirations of its people and the relevant United Nations resolutions," he added.
The president maintained that Pakistan has always respected and supported the national sovereignty of Afghanistan despite historical differences over the years.
However, he lamented that the Afghan Taliban regime was allowing and supporting a "cocktail of terror groups" to use their soil for launching attacks against neighbouring countries, including Pakistan.
He also criticised Kabul for collaborating with India in launching terror attacks against Pakistani civilians and security personnel.
In his message, PM Shehbaz described it as an "immense honour and pride" for the country that the struggle for independence was led by Quaid-e-Azam, Allama Muhammad Iqbal and many other distinguished leaders.
"Our forefathers endured immense hardships and made unparalleled sacrifices, ultimately bringing the struggle for freedom to a successful conclusion," he said.
The prime minister maintained that the journey of national development and prosperity was "thriving ahead towards a brighter future" despite the challenges along the way.
According to PM Shehbaz, the people of Pakistan have achieved remarkable success in every sphere of life despite numerous difficulties.
Detailing the government's performance, he said that the country has successfully navigated through extremely challenging circumstances and achieved the objective of economic stability over the last two and a half years.
"We are now moving steadily towards the goal of a developed economy. During the past two years, remittances of overseas Pakistanis have increased by $11.3 billion, reflecting their continued confidence in the policies of the government," he added.
The premier said that harnessing modern information technology, promoting innovation-driven sustainable industrial and agricultural development and skills development remained among the government's foremost priorities.
He also lauded the armed forces for ensuring that Pakistan's defence remains invincible, saying the nation took immense pride in its valiant armed forces.
During Marka-e-Haq, the armed forces, under the leadership of Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, demonstrated exemplary unity, unwavering resolve and extraordinary courage, the premier said.
Pakistan remains committed to making any sacrifice for the defence of the country and to vigorously defend its national interests, including its inalienable right to water resources, he added.
Amid the complex and challenging regional situation, Pakistan has played a constructive role as a responsible nation and as a stabilising force in promoting global peace, stability and regional cooperation.
The prime minister said that the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye was a testament to Islamabad's effective role in the region and its emerging strategic strength.
He also expressed solidarity with the oppressed Palestinian people and with brothers and sisters in IIOJK, reiterating steadfast principled support for them.
"Lasting peace in South Asia hinges on diplomatic resolution of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with the relevant United Nations resolutions, international law and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people," he said.
PM Shehbaz paid tribute to all the martyrs who sacrificed their lives for the beloved homeland, saying the nation owed a profound debt of gratitude to brave armed forces, courageous personnel of law enforcement agencies, and all those martyrs.
"Let us, on this day, renew our national resolve to work together for the development and prosperity, peace and stability, mutual harmony and national unity," he said.
The premier extended an invitation to all the segments of society and political parties to "join hands and work constructively together" for the national integrity and for the protection and advancement of national interests.
United Arab Emirates (UAE) President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan congratulated President Zardari on the occasion of Independence Day.
UAE Vice President, Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, and Vice President, Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the Presidential Court Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan sent similar messages to President Zardari and PM Shehbaz on the occasion, according Wam news agency.

title: Balochistan home minister's security convoy comes under fire in Mastung
description: Convoy was travelling from Kalat towards Quetta.Six injured security personnel shifted to hospital.Security personnel exchanged fire with attackers.QUETTA: Balochistan Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langau's security convoy came...
author: Ataullah Baloch
content:
Published August 14, 2026
QUETTA: Balochistan Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langau’s security convoy came under fire while travelling from Kalat to Quetta, officials said on Friday.
Mastung additional deputy commissioner said the convoy was targeted while travelling towards Quetta, while police said Langau remained safe in the firing.
At least six personnel from the security squad were injured in the exchange of fire, according to police.
The injured personnel were shifted to Nawab Ghous Bakhsh Hospital in Quetta for treatment, police said.
Speaking after the attack, the Balochistan home minister vowed that the attack will not weaken their resolve. "I cannot be frightened by these firecrackers," Langau said while speaking in Quetta.
The incident came around three weeks after a sessions judge and his gunman were killed when unidentified assailants opened fire on their vehicle in Mastung.
An additional sessions judge and another person were also critically injured in the attack, an official said on July 23.
According to District Police Officer (DPO) Allah Bakhsh Baloch, the judges were travelling from Quetta to the sessions court in Mastung when their vehicle came under fire in the Wali Khan area.
Pakistan witnessed a surge in terror activities, particularly in its Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, since 2021, when the Afghan Taliban came into power.
According to a report by the Centre for Research and Security Studies (CRSS), the two provinces remained the country's main hotspots for violence during the second quarter of 2026, with KP emerging as the worst-affected region.
The report stated that KP and Balochistan together accounted for nearly 96% of all violence-related fatalities recorded during the quarter. Of the total deaths, more than 61% (475) were reported in KP, while Balochistan accounted for 34% (265).
KP also recorded the highest number of violent incidents, with 151 cases, representing 57% of the nationwide total. Balochistan followed with 94 incidents, or 35%, underscoring the concentration of militant activity in the two provinces.

title: Unauthorised traveller sites expanding as population grows
description: The government says such developments are unacceptable â so why do they keep springing up?
author: Ben Schofield
content:
This site in Wickford, Essex, only has permission for seven mobile homes
The number of unauthorised Gypsy and traveller sites is on the rise, with developments often carried out over Bank Holiday weekends.
Since April, sites in Hertfordshire, Essex, Cambridgeshire, Bedfordshire and elsewhere have been transformed, prompting legal battles and local dismay.
In January, the number of unauthorised traveller caravans â those without planning permission â across England stood at 4,950, a 73% increase on January 2020's figure of 2,860.
The summer count also shows a rise, of 44% between July 2019 and July 2025, from 3,113 to 4,471.
A senior councillor in one affected area warns there has been a "loss of control" of the planning system, while villagers living near one site likened its rapid construction to a "military operation" .
The government says unauthorised development is "totally unacceptable" and that councils have "strong powers" to tackle it.
But Cliff Codona, who founded and chairs the National Travellers' Action Group, says the planning system is like a "big dagger in their back" for travellers, leaving them no option but to "break the law".
So what do travellers say is driving some to act unlawfully, and what do others think?
Clifford Codona now lives with his family near Wisbech, Cambridgeshire
When Codona moved on to what has become his family's caravan site, just outside Elm, near Wisbech, Cambridgeshire, in 2020, he did not have planning permission.
"We pulled down on a Friday evening when we knew the council was all closed up and we just took it for granted that this is how things get done," he recalls.
"As soon as they know you're a Gypsy," he says, a planning application is "stopped â dead in its tracks".
Codona did not have planning permission when he first moved on to his current plot
After starting work at their site, Codona and family made a "part-retrospective" planning application that was later approved by a planning committee, despite the parish council saying it was an "unsustainable location".
He says they have worked hard to be good neighbours, but admits "to put a Gypsy site here is very naughty".
Codona claims to have been evicted 50 times in his life, which he says was "horrific" and like going through "hell and back".
"We've broke the law â I'll admit to you here today I've done everything... to live on land and get permission to be there," he says.
Codona, pictured in 2002, claims to have been evicted 50 times, including from this site near Hatch, Bedfordshire
Codona, who has Gypsy and travelling showman heritage, recalls that travellers would acquire land in "covert" ways.
"We would have to put a raincoat on, sunglasses or whatever, slide ourselves into an auction [and] wait for the property to come up for sale."
More recently, online auctions are "even better... fantastic" for travellers, he says.
Codona says there is more need for Gypsy and traveller caravans because the population is increasing
Codona, who has 14 grandchildren and a great-grandchild, says more caravans are the result of a growing Gypsy and traveller population .
In July 2019, councils across England counted 23,636 traveller caravans.
By July 2025, there were 28,659 â a 21% increase.
But the number of caravans without planning permission rose much faster.
George Jeffery put forward a motion calling for council officials to "pursue all lawful and proportionate compliance options" against the development at Newlands Road
Last summer, officials in Basildon, Essex, counted more unauthorised caravans than anywhere else in England.
Between July 2019 and July 2025, the number of unauthorised caravans in Basildon rose 164%.
Its winter count showed a year-on-year fall between 2025 and 2026, but up 14% compared to January 2020.
George Jeffery, a Conservative member of the local council's cabinet, fears a "lack of enforcement" means the authority has been seen as a "soft touch".
The borough has had to deal with the issue before.
Eighty families were forcibly evicted from a site at Dale Farm in an operation that concluded almost 15 years ago .
Jeffery does not rule out needing to call on "police resources to keep the peace" once again.
"Basildon should be robust and tackle it head on and not be afraid to use the full extent of the powers available to it," he says.
He does not want to highlight any particular community and says he is against all unauthorised building.
He has highlighted a site at the end of Newlands Road, Wickford, that has flouted planning laws for years.
It had permission for one static and one touring caravan but building work took place between around 2018 and 2022.
Basildon Borough Council issued planning enforcement notices but was challenged at a public inquiry.
A planning inspector ruled five caravans could stay across two plots, giving 16 months for the remaining caravans, hardstanding and part of a road to go.
That deadline passed in July 2025, but more than a dozen caravans and infrastructure remain.
On 3 August, the council granted permission for two more mobile homes on one other plot.
Land Registry records show the site has been divided up and sold to several owners.
One plot changed hands in June for a reported Â£100,000.
What does the law say about unauthorised encampments?
Some people living near Newlands Road said they were now struggling to sell their homes.
Neighbours have complained about fires and for months there was a constant hum from electrical generators.
Jeffery believes there is a "two-tier planning system", with rules applied unfairly.
There have been fires on the site in 2022 (left) and 2025 (right)
In November, he proposed a council motion, which was amended before being passed, asking officials to draw up proposals for a "full range of enforcement routes" for the site.
The council is considering applying for a court injunction to force the owners and occupants to comply with the enforcement notices.
The BBC has made efforts to contact the owners and occupants but has received no response.
The council said it could not comment "as doing so could prejudice ongoing legal enforcement proceedings".
Matthew Green said councils should make sure there are enough pitches for Gypsies and travellers in their areas
Matthew Green, a planning consultant who represented one of the site's residents at the 2023 planning inquiry, says councils could "get an injunction and get the people removed" if enforcement notices were not complied with.
"But," he asks, "if they go somewhere, where do they go?
"The answer is fairly straightforward: the council have to ensure â as is their duty â that there are enough pitches with planning permission in their area to meet the needs of people residing in their area."
In a report from February, council officials said there was a "shortfall" in the supply of "suitable and deliverable Gypsy and traveller sites" in Basildon.
The borough has not updated its local plan, which guides new development, since 1999, prompting intervention , external from the housing minister last month.
In 2024, analysts concluded , external that by 2042 Basildon would need enough pitches to house 302 Gypsy and traveller households.
Between April 2023 and February 2026, permission was granted for 31 new Gypsy and traveller pitches.
After a planning appeal decision in 2024, only plots 1 and 3 (left) at the Newlands Road site had planning permission, along with an access road to plot 3 (shown in green, right), while the remaining plots did not. Plot 2 was given permission for two mobile homes on 3 August
But Green advises it is "foolish" to develop land without permission because it "reduces... chances" of getting work eventually approved.
The government is looking at strengthening national planning policy on "intentional unauthorised development", particularly for retrospective planning applications.
A spokesperson for the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government said it was "important that all Gypsy and traveller communities have access to safe, suitable sites â and councils must ensure they meet the needs of the community in their area".
"We're also clear that unauthorised developments are completely unacceptable, and we've given councils like Basildon strong powers to tackle these including working closely with the police and taking court action."
For Codona, who is now living a quieter life, surrounded by his family, there is "no incentive in the planning system" for enough sites to be approved.
But he adds: "We don't want to tell lies; we don't want to break the laws.
"We don't want to move on to bits of land and have hell to pay till we can get to live there."
A council has won a High Court fight over an unauthorised traveller camp in Flamstead

title: AJK elections: PPP, PML-N candidates retain lead in Bagh after repolling
description: Turnout remained low in both constituencies, while polling was held peacefully under adequate security arrangements for polling staff and voters.
author: News Desk, Tariq Naqash
content:
MUZAFFARABAD: Sardar Ziaul Qamar of the PPP and Sardar Mir Akbar of the PML-N retained the lead in their respective constituencies in Bagh, after results were received from all 23 polling stations where repolling was held on Saturday.
According to unofficial and unverified results, Qamar defeated the PML-N’s Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas in LA-15 (Central Bagh) by 1,891 votes. He secured 17,118 votes against Minhas’s 15,227. Repolling was held at nine polling stations in the constituency.
It was the third consecutive defeat for Minhas in the constituency, who had entered electoral politics in 2016 under the banner of the PML-N, won that election and served as a minister during the following five years.
Qamar, meanwhile, secured his second consecutive victory after winning the 2023 by-election.
In LA-16 (Eastern Bagh), the PML-N’s Akbar defeated the PPP’s Sardar Qamaruz Zaman by 3,833 votes, securing 20,796 votes against his rival’s 16,963. Repolling was held at 14 polling stations in the constituency.
Akbar has won four elections previously, making Saturday’s victory his fifth overall and third consecutive win.
According to local journalists, Akbar’s sustained presence in his constituency, where he regularly attends celebrations, is believed to have contributed to his popularity. Constituents said he was known for attending even occasions marking the death of villagers’ livestock.
Turnout remained low in both constituencies, according to witnesses, with voters at some polling stations “voluntarily” opting not to cast their ballots.
Polling was, however, held peacefully, with adequate security arrangements for polling staff and voters. Polling officials described the conduct of voters towards them and security personnel as cordial.
“Though no voters showed up [at some polling stations], the attitude and cooperation of local notables with polling staff and security forces was exemplary, including arrangements for their accommodation and meals,” said a presiding officer in LA-15.
The repolling results took the PML-N’s tally to 25 seats and the PPP’s to 12 in the AJK Legislative Assembly. Sajid Iqbal Abbasi, who won LA-14 (Dhirkot) against Muslim Conference president and former AJK premier Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan by a large margin, also reportedly decided to support the PML-N.
In the third phase of polling on Monday, PPP’s Qamar secured 16,637 votes in LA-15 (Bagh Central), followed by PML-N’s Minhas with 15,015 and Jamaat-i-Islami’s retired Brig Dr Muhammad Khan with 12,259. But as polling could not be held at nine stations in the constituency, the commission withheld the result.
Similarly, the result of LA-16 (Eastern Bagh) was also withheld after polling could not be held at 14 stations, which have a combined 7,238 registered voters.
Results from the remaining polling stations showed that PML-N’s Akbar, who secured 19,515 votes, was leading his closest rival, PPP’s Zaman, by 3,225 votes.
In both constituencies, all five candidates had accused their opponents of rigging.
Meanwhile, the AJK Election Commission notified AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore as the returned candidate from LA-17. The notification was issued late on Friday and was provided to the media on Saturday.
LA-17 (Haveli), where Rathore was contesting from, emerged as the most contentious constituency during the third phase of the polls on Monday. The election was thrown into fresh controversy on Wednesday after the returning officer issued the Form 27 declaring him the winner despite an assurance, according to his PML-N rival Engr Mohsin Aziz, that the result would not be announced until his complaint was taken up by the Election Commission.
Aziz subsequently challenged the election, with the AJK Chief Election Co­­mmissioner (CEC) retired Justice Ghulam Mustafa Mughal on Thursday reserving his decision after hearing arguments from both sides.
On Saturday, the Election Commission said that it would announce the verdict on the petitions at 5pm.
The PML-N bagged 24 seats — nine from Mirpur division in the first phase on July 27 and 15 in the second phase on Aug 2 comprising Muzaffarabad Division and the 12 refugee seats. The PPP, on the other hand, won only 10 constituencies during these phases.
The polls are being held in phases amid unrest in the region.
The third phase, held on Monday, was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district. However, the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation.
On Monday, polls went ahead in Bagh and Haveli, but the Election Commission later withheld the results of two constituencies pending repolling at 23 polling stations.
It announced the result for LA-14 (Bagh-I), commonly known as Dhirkot, where Jammu Kashmir Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party candidate Sajid Iqbal Abbasi secured a landslide victory with 40,522 votes.

title: JI announces countrywide protest against petroleum levy on Sunday
description: JI chief warns that any government attempt to obstruct the protest could turn the campaign for lower petrol prices into a movement to topple the government.
author: Ahmad Fraz Khan
content:
LAHORE: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) Pakistan Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman on Saturday announced that the party would stage sit-ins outside the Governor Houses in Karachi, Quetta and Peshawar and the Chief Minister House in Lahore on Sunday against the levy imposed on petroleum products and other taxes.
The sit-ins would begin at 4pm, he said, adding that participants would march from different cities to reach the designated sites.
Addressing a packed press conference at Mansoora alongside the party’s central and provincial office-bearers, Rehman said, “We want to convey the voice of suppressed labourers, students and other sections of society to the government peacefully.”
He warned that if the government tried to create trouble or interfere with the protest, the campaign for lower petrol prices could turn into a movement to topple the government.
The JI emir said the party had organised sit-ins at 510 locations the previous week and that “not a single flowerpot was broken” during the protests. “We will come peacefully and return after securing our right,” he said.
The JI chief said that “we are giving the time for the start of the sit-ins but not for their ending”, adding that the party was demanding that the petrol price be fixed at Rs225 after abolishing the levy, while the price of roti be fixed at Rs10 and those of flour, electricity and gas be reduced.
He also called for cuts in flour, electricity and gas prices and demanded that vehicles used by federal and provincial bureaucrats, judges, ministers, advisers and others should not have engine capacities exceeding 1,300cc.
The JI leader further demanded an end to free electricity, gas, fuel and other “extravagant privileges”, saying the taxes collected from the public should be spent on the people.
He alleged that the government was meeting its expenses at the expense of citizens’ hard-earned money, while the rulers were unwilling to give up their privileges.
“Rs130 is being collected per litre of petrol as extortion in the name of the levy,” he alleged.
Rehman also claimed that federal government expenditure had been estimated at Rs800 billion but had reached Rs1 trillion.
He questioned the government’s priorities, alleging that public transport remained unavailable while the Punjab chief minister was travelling in an aircraft worth Rs11bn.
“If the masses will not come out now, then at what point will they leave their homes?” he asked.
The JI emir said his party had no personal agenda and always raised issues concerning the public. He warned that the party had a “second plan” if the government attempted to stop the protests, saying the sit-ins would then be expanded across the country.
JI Deputy Chiefs Liaqat Baloch, Mian Muhammad Aslam and Dr Attaur Rehman, Acting Secretary General Nazeer Ahmed Janjua, Deputy Secretary Azhar Iqbal Hassan, Lahore Emir Ziauddin Ansari, Central Punjab Secretary Babar Rashid, social media head Salman Sheikh, and JI Youth representatives Ahmad Salman Baloch and Jibran Butt were also present at the press conference.

title: Rescuers search for survivors as Indonesian 7.7 quake death toll rises to 47
description: Nearly 160 houses, dozens of educational and health facilities and other public buildings damaged when the earthquake struck.
author: AFP
content:
Rescuers combed through debris for survivors on Saturday after a powerful earthquake struck off Indonesia’s eastern Flores island, killing at least 47 people, according to disaster officials.
The national disaster management agency (BNPB) raised the death toll from 40 late on Saturday, while rescue official Fathur Rahman said 50 people were injured in the 7.7-magnitude quake.
Suharyanto, who leads the BNPB, said earlier that people were trapped in several buildings.
“These will be the initial targets of the disaster response teams,” he said.
Nearly 160 houses, dozens of educational and health facilities and other public buildings were damaged when the earthquake struck the popular tourist island in Indonesia’s east, the BNPB reported.
The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said preparations were underway to bring aid to some 2,000 people in temporary shelters.
The government sent 50,000 aid packages weighing a total of 275 tonnes to the area, and European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen offered help from the bloc’s Copernicus Earth observation satellites.
“Europe stands ready to deploy Copernicus, our eyes in the sky, to support search and rescue efforts. Indonesia, we stand with you,” she wrote on X.
“I have never felt an earthquake this big,” Yulian Juita Ekalia, who lives in Ruteng city — more than 100 kilometres west of the epicentre — told AFP by telephone hours after the tremor.
“It felt like we were on a trampoline; it was really scary,” said the 37-year-old university lecturer, who was jolted awake at around 5:30am (2130 GMT on Friday).
“As I rushed to get outside, everything in the house fell down: the television, my son’s trophies, the dish racks, suitcases on top of the wardrobes. When I got outside, my son and neighbours were already there, screaming in fear.”
Rescue official Fathur told AFP the focus was on locating victims who may be buried under rubble, but rescue efforts have been complicated by landslides cutting off roads. Many Flores inhabitants were left without electricity and telecommunications.
Residents in Nagekeo, an area close to the epicentre, raced for higher ground as the sea retreated early Saturday — a possible sign of an approaching tsunami, AFP journalists witnessed.
While a tsunami warning was lifted, authorities urged people not to return to damaged buildings for fear that aftershocks may bring them down.
Hundreds remained outside hours later as dozens of aftershocks shook the island, the strongest measured at a magnitude of 6.1.
Waves of up to 1.6 metres were reported in some coastal regions of Flores, according to Indonesia’s BMKG geological agency.
Yulian said she had dragged her stove outside and was cooking there, fearing further tremors. She said she saw patients being treated under emergency tents outside a nearby hospital.
Nagekeo resident Yohanes Babo, 56, said he was at a market when the earth started shaking in the early morning hours.
“The shaking was strong. Thankfully, we were already outside the house,” he told AFP . “People were panicking, running here and there. We’re evacuating for the time being… and trying to get to the hills.”
The epicentre of the shallow quake was located just off the north coast of the island, US and Indonesian authorities said. The affected areas have few, if any, high-rise buildings.
A second, deep onland quake was measured at a magnitude of 6.9 near Pematangsiantar on Sumatra island — thousands of kilometres away — some 12 hours after the Flores tremor.
There were no initial reports of damage or casualties, and no tsunami alert was issued.
Indonesia experiences frequent earthquakes due to its location in the Pacific “Ring of Fire”, an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin.
Flores was struck by a 7.7-magnitude earthquake in 1992, which triggered a tsunami and resulted in around 2,500 deaths.
A devastating 9.1-magnitude tremor in 2004 struck off the coast of Sumatra and triggered a tsunami that killed 220,000 throughout the region, about 170,000 of them in Indonesia, in one of the deadliest natural disasters in recorded history.
President Asif Ali Zardari expressed deep sorrow over the loss of lives in the earthquake.
“On behalf of the people of Pakistan, the President extended heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and expressed solidarity with the Government and people of Indonesia in this difficult hour.”
He further said that Pakistan was ready to extend all possible assistance.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said he was “deeply saddened” by the loss of life and destruction caused by the earthquake.
He extended his heartfelt condolences to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and the people of Indonesia and the bereaved families on behalf of the government and the Pakistani public.
“Our thoughts and prayers are with all those affected, and we pray for the swift recovery of the injured,” he wrote on X. “Pakistan stands shoulder to shoulder with the brotherly people of Indonesia and wishes strength and resilience to all those facing this difficult time.”

title: Armed Forces congratulate nation on Independence Day
description: Armed Forces pay tribute to Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah: ISPR.ISPR says Armed Forces reaffirmed resolve to defend territorial integrity.Military urges Pakistanis to uphold principles of Faith, Unity and Discipline.ISLAMABAD:...
author: Web Desk
content:
Published August 14, 2026
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan's armed forces have extended heartfelt felicitations to the nation on the country's 79 years of independence, reaffirming their resolve to defend the country's sovereignty, uphold the Constitution and safeguard its national interests, a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Friday.
The joint message was issued by Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf and Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu on behalf of the Armed Forces of Pakistan.
The military leadership paid tribute to Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the country's founding fathers and all those whose sacrifices led to the creation of Pakistan, the military's media wing said.
It said their vision, courage and determination remained a guiding force for the nation and continued to inspire Pakistanis to uphold the country's principles and ideals.
The Armed Forces also paid tribute to the country's martyrs, veterans, law enforcement personnel and all Pakistanis who have served the nation.
Their courage and selfless service had strengthened Pakistan's resilience and helped safeguard its independence, security and national interests, the statement said.
The military leadership reaffirmed its commitment to defending the country's sovereignty and territorial integrity against all threats while upholding the Constitution and fulfilling the trust placed in the armed forces by the people.
It said the armed forces, together with the nation, would remain committed to preserving peace and stability and creating conditions conducive to national progress and prosperity.
"As guardians of Pakistan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, the Armed Forces reaffirm their unwavering resolve to defend the motherland against all threats, uphold the Constitution and discharge the sacred trust reposed in them by the people of Pakistan," it said.
The military leadership said Pakistan's strength lay in the unity and collective resolve of its people.
It called on the nation to renew its commitment to the principles of Faith, Unity and Discipline, strengthen national cohesion, promote tolerance and work towards a secure, stable and prosperous Pakistan.
The statement concluded with messages of solidarity with the nation and Pakistan, with these words: "Pakistan Armed Forces Zindabad! Pakistan Hamesha Paindabad!"
